LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Patriots vs. Bears Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook New England Patriots vs. Chicago Bears UNDER 50.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Drake Maye OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (-116) – Peter Dewey Colston Loveland Anytime TD (+170) – Peter Dewey D’Andre Swift UNDER 61.5 Rushing Yards (-115) – Peter Dewey This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this matchup in his Road to 272 column , where he picks every game of the NFL season. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Bears tight end Colston Loveland had a breakout showing in Week 6, catching six of his seven targets for 65 yards and a score. Williams only threw one touchdown in Week 6, but Loveland was targeted multiple times in the end zone – Caleb just missed him for a second score. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. Even if the volume is there for the veteran back, I think he’s a fade candidate in Week 7. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. home.blurb: Injury Report Analysis: Patriots rule out five players for Thursday Night Football vs. the Bears Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS The Patriots ruled out CB Carlton Davis III (neck), G Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), G Ben Brown (knee), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring) for Thursday night in Chicago. On Wednesday, the Patriots ruled out LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), RG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots are also listing RT Morgan Moses (foot), S Kevin Byard III (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder), and LB Christian Ellliss (chest) as questionable for Thursday night's game. Starting on offense, the Patriots offensive line will be shorthanded, with the Pats down multiple guards who have started games this season. Along with starting RG Mike Onwenu (ankle) and top backup Greg Van Roten (thigh), who are on injured reserve, New England is also down Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Brown (knee). In his final press conference before Thursday night's game, head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed that Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will start vs. the Bears. The Pats projected starting offensive line is LT Will Campbell, LG Walter Rouse, C Jared Wilson, RG Matt Pryor, and RT Morgan Moses (questionable) or Caleb Lomu. If Moses can't finish the game and the Patriots start Lomu at guard, the rookie would need to kick back outside. Vrabel also hinted at Lomu being prepared to be the backup center. In short, that's a lot of moving parts to plan for in-game contingencies, so the clearest path forward is to start Rouse and Pryor at guard while Lomu continues in his role as the top swing tackle. Plus, Moses is listed as questionable, and if he doesn't play on the short week, Lomu would make his first NFL start at right tackle. At the skill positions, the Patriots are down two wide receivers, Doubs and Hollins, both on injured reserve. However, the Pats will have top WR A.J. Brown, whose ankle is off the injury report. New England's available wideouts are Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III, while OC Josh McDaniels can use all his tight ends and running backs. The Patriots could elevate a fifth wide receiver from the practice squad, but that feels unlikely with limited game-day roster spots. Moving over to the defense, starting CB Carlton Davis III (neck) will need to wait at least another week before returning to the lineup. Despite practicing in a limited capacity this week, Davis won't play on Thursday night, marking the third straight game he has missed with his neck injury (four out of the last six). The Patriots held lighter walkthrough sessions during a short week to prepare for the Bears, so Davis may have participated as a ramp-up for a potential return sooner rather than later. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Baltimore Ravens The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset. Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23 New York Giants (+10) at Houston Texans Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23 Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21 Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Rams 28, Raiders 27 Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17 Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles (+4.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close. Pick: Cowboys 21, Eagles 20 New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. The game will be held at the multi-purpose facility in the suburbs of Paris. Pittsburgh was an early 3.5-point favorite on Monday. Things have changed, as the Steelers have been slipped a bit to a 3-point favorite as of Saturday morning. Here are our picks Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 31-17 This is a unpredictable game that could go either way without considering both teams' records. However, the New Orleans Saints' defense does not inspire confidence in stopping the Pittsburgh Steelers. Aaron Rodgers remains a solid quarterback at age 42, passing for nearly 1,500 yards with 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. Allowing 377 passing yards to Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy does not bode well for New Orleans. While the win over the New York Giants was notable, New York lacked a running back like Jaylen Warren to keep the Saints' defense honest. Warren has rushed for 460 yards on 84 carries, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt. His ability to gain yards after contact, identify lanes and contribute to the passing game gives Pittsburgh multiple offensive options. That creates a difficult matchup for New Orleans. The Saints allows 138 rushing yards per game, ranking 30th in the NFL, while Pittsburgh averages 99.2 rushing yards per game, ranking 20th. Despite Pittsburgh's modest team average, Warren's efficiency indicates the Steelers can exploit the Saints' rushing defense. For New Orleans to win, its offense must perform consistently throughout the game. The Steelers present a tougher matchup than the Giants and have their starting quarterback available. While Tyler Shough offers New Orleans its primary offensive spark, the offensive line must protect him against T.J. Watt, who excels at pressuring quarterbacks. Pittsburgh also features a stronger pass rush and secondary than New York. Steelers 31 Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 28-21 After getting their collective tails chewed out by the team owner a week and a half ago, the Saints put together a better effort in a win at the New York Football Giants last weekend. Now, after a week in the mother country (at least the one for New Orleans and its state), players and coaches alike are saying this is the best week of practice the team has had all season. Meanwhile, a visibly exhausted Aaron Rodgers spoke to the media on Thursday, the day his Pittsburgh Steelers arrived in Paris, worried about jet lag and getting to France so late in the week. True, the Steelers are favored, and rightfully so with a flip-flop record of 4-2 compared to the Saints. But this game seems more and more like a home game for New Orleans fans as even Harry's New York Bar "changed its name" for one day to celebrate the team and its fans. Harry's New York Bar becomes Harry's New Orleans Bar for one day. | Harry's New York Bar Instagram There is, of course, the immediate retort that home field advantage is a myth for this program. And if you thought that, you'd be correct, as the Saints haven't won at home since December 21, 2025. However, most of us didn't see the turnaround this team did in a week. Add to that, the team's ability to acclimate to a different time zone, and Pittsburgh's lack thereof, and I see a Saints victory. Pittsburgh has playoff expectations in the 2026 season, and new head coach Mike McCarthy has his team at a 4-2 start through six weeks. However, the AFC North has four teams over .500, putting the Steelers in a spot where they can't afford many losses early in the season. Meanwhile, New Orleans is off to a 2-4 start, snapping a three-game skid in Week 6 when they beat the New York Giants. Shough and company have performed pretty well on offense, but New Orleans is sitting in third place in the division at just 2-4 through the first six weeks. This is technically a home game for the Saints, and they're set as underdogs against Rodgers and the Steelers. This line opened up 2.5 points (Pittsburgh favored), and it has since moved to three. The Steelers have a top-10 defense in EPA/Play, while the Saints are a bottom-10 unit and sit dead last in the league in EPA/Rush. That could offer some interesting prop spots with the Steelers' backfield of Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren looking pretty strong in their Week 6 win against Tampa Bay. So, how should bettors wager on the NFL’s first-ever game in France? All week long, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player prop selections and a few anytime touchdown scorer choices for this game in Paris. So, why not put all of our favorites in one spot? He’s backing Pittsburgh to cover the spread in Paris as a “road” favorite: The Steelers' run game against the Saints' run defense will be the biggest difference-maker in this game. Pittsburgh has done a great job running the football this season, ranking fifth in rush EPA, and Jaylen Warren is averaging 5.5 yards per carry. Now they face a Saints defense that's last in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate, while also giving up 4.8 yards per rush. If Warren can be effective on the ground, the Saints' offense will struggle to keep pace. The Steelers' defense is top 10 in the NFL in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. Let's hope that defense travels. I'm going to back the Steelers as favorites in France. Saints wide receiver Chris Olave has two touchdowns in the 2026 season, and he’s actually seen his targets drop (13 total in the last two weeks) after four straight double-digit target games to open the season. Despite that, I’m buying low on the former Ohio State star on Sunday. The Steelers have allowed just six passing scores this season and are sixth in the league in EPA/Pass, but Olave has been the focal point of this Saints team that throws the ball almost as much as anyone in the NFL. The Saints are third in the league in pass attempts in 2026, and Olave has drawn 61 looks in six games. There are other options to consider for the Saints (Devaughn Vele, Juwan Johnson), but I’ll gladly take a true No. 1 receiver at nearly 2/1 to find the end zone in Week 7. The Saints have been awful against the run this season, ranking dead last in the NFL in EPA/Rush and allowing 4.8 yards per carry. That’s a great sign for Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren, who is averaging 5.5 yards per carry and already has 460 rushing yards in six games this season. Even with Rico Dowdle (toe) returning to action in Week 6, Warren led the backfield by playing over 74 percent of the snaps and handling 14 carries. He finished the day with 50 rushing yards and 28 receiving yards. While this prop is a little higher than that, Warren had a three-game streak with 90 or more rushing yards snapped in Week 6. Tampa Bay is third in the NFL in EPA/Rush this season, so this is a much easier matchup for Warren in Week 7. He’s handled at least 10 carries in every game, including 14 or more in four straight. Since the veteran has taken the clear lead in this backfield, I expect him to be the biggest beneficiary against this Saints defense. Rookie receiver Germie Bernand has been forced into a bigger role with Pittsburgh's injuries this season, and he’s thriving in it. The second-round pick had nine targets and six catches in Week 5 against Indianapolis, and he followed that up with a massive day in the win against Tampa Bay. Bernard found the end zone for the first time in his career, and he caught 11 of his 12 looks from Rodgers for 87 yards. Since Rodgers isn’t really pushing the ball down the field, I love this receptions prop for Bernand, as he’s emerged as the No. 2 receiver behind DK Metcalf. The rookie played over 91 percent of the snaps in each of the last two weeks, and he’s clearly established a solid rapport with Rodgers. I think he’s a great target against a Saints defense that is in the bottom 10 in the league in EPA/Pass, opponent completions and opponent passing yards in 2026. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Saints Bold Predictions: Offense Puts on a Show Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Pittsburgh Steelers are officially in France and are ready to take on the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris. Riding a two-game win streak heading into Week 7, the Steelers still have things to clean up as they look to keep pace in the race for both the AFC North and one of three Wild Card spots in the conference. Regardless, Pittsburgh is 4-2 for a fourth-straight season and has what some may consider a must-win type of game vs. New Orleans given how tough its schedule gets immediately following its Week 9 bye. With that, here are three bold predictions for the Steelers as they look to take down the Saints. Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) throws a pass during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Put Up 400+ Yards of Offense Steelers Put Up 400+ Yards of Offense Pittsburgh's offense largely falls near the middle of the pack, averaging the 12th-fewest yards (320.5) and the 15th-fewest points (22.8) per game in the league. Those numbers are dragged down quite a bit by the team's poor outing against the New England Patriots in Week 2, however, during which they scored just three points with 235 yards of offense. Under Mike McCarthy, the Steelers have proven that they're at least capable of explosive offensive performances. For example, they scored 30 points with 411 yards in a Week 3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals and put up 34 points in a Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. It's possible that Pittsburgh comes out a bit sluggish against the Saints in Paris after arriving later in the week, but the formula is there for the black and gold to have another huge performance. New Orleans' defense is currently tied with the Arizona Cardinals for the most points allowed per game (29.7) while also giving up the fourth-most yards per contest (377.7). The Saints have struggled to consistently get after the quarterback too, as their 33.2 percent pressure rate (per SumerSports ) is the fourth-worst in the NFL despite having 15 sacks. The Steelers' offense already had their way with one of the worst defenses in the league in the Colts, and there's no reason they can't do the same vs. New Orleans by finishing with over 400 yards of total offense. Pittsburgh Forces Two Turnovers The Saints' offense cannot be taken lightly. Even though first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson has yet to play this season with a hamstring injury, while franchise left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. has been out since Week 3 after undergoing ankle surgery, they are still averaging the 11th-most points (25.3) in the league. At the same time, quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown five interceptions and lost three fumbles while New Orleans as a whole has turned the ball over 12 times , which is tied for the third-most in the NFL. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, has 10 takeaways on the year, which is tied with five other teams for the second-most behind the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks at 11. The Steelers' defense is among the better units in the league, as they allow the sixth-lowest EPA per play (-0.1) and the seventh-fewest yards per game (307.5). New Orleans is capable of doing a little bit of damage, but Pittsburgh's defense has stepped up and largely made the necessary plays when it's needed to. Winning the turnover margin is always crucial, and considering how susceptible the Saints are to giving the ball away, the Steelers will end up with two takeaways in this one. Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker (3) and Pittsburgh Steelers safety Robert Spears-Jennings (28) celebrate after a play during the fourth quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Win by Two Scores Steelers Win by Two Scores Pittsburgh is short-handed along the interior of its defensive line with Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) joining Derrick Harmon (foot) on the reserve/injured list. The same can be said at wide receiver, as Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are on IR as well while Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss his second-straight game . Cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) will be sidelined too, and there are also some questions about Rico Dowdle's (knee) availability after he was deemed questionable to suit up on the Steelers' final injury report of the week. Still, this is a game the Steelers should win. Again, maybe they aren't at tip-top shape playing overseas, but they're simply the better and more talented team. The Saints are not a pushover by any means and have the potential to make things tough for Pittsburgh, as evidenced by their comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 2. That being said, New Orleans is 2-4 for a reason. Its defense is among the worst in the league, and while its offense is a formidable unit, it's going to have a tough time keeping up with the Steelers. After notching their first two-score win of the season in Week 5 vs. Indianapolis, who profiles similarly to the Saints, Pittsburgh will do so once again in France and move to 5-2. away.headline: Saints vs. Steelers: Final Week 7 injury report updates key starters
away.blurb: Week 7 starts out with the 2-4 New Orleans Saints and the 4-2 Pittsburgh Steelers facing off in the first ever NFL game played in Paris, France. The Saints left for France immediately after their game at the New York Giants last Sunday. Pittsburgh elected a different approach, arriving in Paris on a red-eye flight early Friday morning. Here is the final injury report for both teams. For the first time this season, the Saints have not ruled out a player on a Friday before a game. Right guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd (illness) are both listed as questionable. Shepherd did not participate at all in team activities on Friday. He has missed the last two games with an illness. Ruiz left last week's victory over the Giants late in the first half with a knee injury and did not return. He had missed practice all of this week until returning in limited duties on Friday. Rookie fourth round choice Jeremiah Wright replaced Ruiz in the lineup against the Giants and played well. Rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson, the team's first round pick, made the trip to Paris but has not been activated off injured reserve. With the Saints on a bye next week, Tyson could return in Week 9. New Orleans does expect linebacker and defensive captain Kaden Elliss to play against the Steelers. Elliss has missed the last three games with a calf injury but returned to practice this week and was a full participant on Friday. Kicker Daniel Carlson also returned to the team, flying into France later in the week. Carlson and his wife are expecting a baby, explaining his late arrival to France. Running back Alvin Kamara, dealing with a back injury, was limited in practice all week but does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) and cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) are both listed as out for the Steelers. Running back Rico Dowdle is dealing with a knee injury and saw only limited practice duty all week. He's listed as questionable. Also listed as questionable is safety DeShon Elliott, dealing with a knee injury but a full practice participant most of the week. Taken off the injury report for the Steelers is pass rusher Alex Highsmith, who was limited most of this week with a groin injury but returned to full duties on Friday. away.headline: T.J. Watt Injured Before Steelers’ Paris Game
away.blurb: Which made superstar edge rusher T.J. Watt’s sudden appearance on the Injury Report quite the concerning update. The top-paid defender missed a previous practice due to rest, but the latest report from the organization classified him as a limited participant due to a calf injury. The team did not include any type of game designation for Watt, although they did rule out wide receiver Ben Skowronek and cornerback Brandin Echols for their Week 7 matchup. This is now the second star edge rusher to appear on the injury report this week. The team’s other starter, Alex Highsmith, popped up on the Injury Report with a groin injury. The injury reduced him to a limited participant in practice ahead of their international contest. Now, Watt is working through his own ailment. It’s good news that the organization hasn’t ruled him out, but how healthy he is entering Week 7 is under serious question. away.headline: Final injury report for Steelers-Saints: Will TJ Watt, Alvin Kamara play?
away.blurb: Of course, Watt missed Wednesday’s practice and was limited in Thursday’s practice due to a calf injury but he is off the injury report and will play after fully practicing Friday. Pittsburgh has listed running back Rico Dowdle as questionable due to a knee injury and he is in danger of missing his first game since returning from a toe injury last week. The Steelers have also listed safety DeShon Elliott as questionable due to a knee injury while cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) and wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out. Of course, Kamara was limited in practice throughout the week as he continues to deal with a back injury, but he is off the injury report and will play against the Steelers. New Orleans has listed guard Cesar Ruiz as questionable due to a knee injury while defensive tackle Nathan Shepard is questionable with an illness. The Pittsburgh Steelers are in Paris Sunday morning as they face off against the New Orleans Saints in a Week 7 interconference matchup. Pittsburgh enters Sunday’s contest with a 4-2 record after defeating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road in overtime in Week 6. Aaron Rodgers led the way for the Steelers in their victory over the Buccaneers as he ended the game with 253 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and an interception while DK Metcalf recorded 93 receiving yards. The Steelers will try to grab another victory Sunday as they face off against the Saints in a tough matchup. New Orleans enters Sunday’s game with a 2-4 record after defeating the New York Giants on the road in Week 6. In their victory over the Giants, Tyler Shough led the way for the Saints as he recorded 176 total yards and four total touchdowns while Kendre Miller added 70 rushing yards. While both teams are looking to pick up a victory in Sunday morning’s matchup, each may be without multiple key players due to injuries. Steelers Injury Report: Will T.J. Watt, Rico Dowdle Play? The Steelers have four players listed on their injury report, though linebacker T.J. Watt is not one of them. If Dowdle is sidelined, Travis Homer could be in line for an increased role behind Jaylen Warren. Saints Injury Report: Will Alvin Kamara Play? The Saints have only two players listed on their injury report, though running back Alvin Kamara is not one of them. home.headline: Saints vs. Steelers: Final Week 7 injury report updates key starters
home.blurb: Week 7 starts out with the 2-4 New Orleans Saints and the 4-2 Pittsburgh Steelers facing off in the first ever NFL game played in Paris, France. The Saints left for France immediately after their game at the New York Giants last Sunday. Pittsburgh elected a different approach, arriving in Paris on a red-eye flight early Friday morning. Here is the final injury report for both teams. For the first time this season, the Saints have not ruled out a player on a Friday before a game. Right guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd (illness) are both listed as questionable. Shepherd did not participate at all in team activities on Friday. He has missed the last two games with an illness. Ruiz left last week's victory over the Giants late in the first half with a knee injury and did not return. He had missed practice all of this week until returning in limited duties on Friday. Rookie fourth round choice Jeremiah Wright replaced Ruiz in the lineup against the Giants and played well. Rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson, the team's first round pick, made the trip to Paris but has not been activated off injured reserve. With the Saints on a bye next week, Tyson could return in Week 9. New Orleans does expect linebacker and defensive captain Kaden Elliss to play against the Steelers. Elliss has missed the last three games with a calf injury but returned to practice this week and was a full participant on Friday. Kicker Daniel Carlson also returned to the team, flying into France later in the week. Carlson and his wife are expecting a baby, explaining his late arrival to France. Running back Alvin Kamara, dealing with a back injury, was limited in practice all week but does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) and cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) are both listed as out for the Steelers. Running back Rico Dowdle is dealing with a knee injury and saw only limited practice duty all week. He's listed as questionable. Also listed as questionable is safety DeShon Elliott, dealing with a knee injury but a full practice participant most of the week. Taken off the injury report for the Steelers is pass rusher Alex Highsmith, who was limited most of this week with a groin injury but returned to full duties on Friday. home.headline: 5 injuries to monitor during the New Orleans Saints' bye week
home.blurb: Etienne is also managing a hamstring injury, and he's eligible to return as soon as the Saints get back on the practice field after the bye. The question is whether or not he'll be ready. We've seen New Orleans take a patient approach with Tyson, and it's likely they'll do the same for Etienne. He's the best athlete in their backfield and they signed him with intentions of spearheading the run game. What's frustrating is that the rushing attack struggled with and without him. Hopefully Etienne can return soon and make a positive impact in the second half of the season. Ruiz practiced on a limited basis late last week but couldn't dress out for the game in Paris, so his arrow seems to be trending up. Like it or not, the Saints need him. Rookie fourth-round pick Jeremiah Wright hasn't been up to replacing the veteran starter. He was outmatched physically by Steelers vet Keeanu Benton and has been a weak link in pass protection, yielding three pressures, a sack, and a penalty on 55 snaps through two games. Ruiz has given up four pressures, no sacks, and two penalties (one offsetting) through 261 snaps this season. The Saints haven't been able to run behind him either. That doesn't mean Wright won't or can't develop into a quality starter, but he's got a long ways to go. Reid couldn't finish the Steelers game after entering the NFL's concussion protocol, but the bye week does give him more time to recover. We'll see if it makes a difference when the Saints get back on the practice field next week. These brain injuries are difficult to diagnose and return from. Every situation is different; we've seen players get cleared in time for their next game or miss most of a month (like Taysom Hill did in 2021) after a scary hit. Let's hope Reid is resting up and getting well. Donaldson outsnapped Kendre Miller 4-to-1 on the team's first drive (Alvin Kamara was on the field six times) before exiting with a shoulder injury. It's unclear if it was the same shoulder that limited him at practice during the week, but he did upgrade to full reps before the game. Whether or not he aggravated that shoulder injury remains to be seen but it's a reasonable conclusion. Who else can return from injured reserve? The Saints have already used four of their eight allotted return slots, so only four more players can come back from injured reserve during the regular season (if they manage to reach the playoffs, they'll get two more return slots). They already reactivated linebacker Jaylan Ford, defensive back Lorenzo Styles Jr., and long snapper Zach Wood, with Tyson designated to return once he's able. That leaves the only players eligible to return from injured reserve as Etienne and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. Assuming they both get the designated-to-return tag, that leaves New Orleans with just two more return slots for the rest of the season. home.blurb: Of course, Watt missed Wednesday’s practice and was limited in Thursday’s practice due to a calf injury but he is off the injury report and will play after fully practicing Friday. Pittsburgh has listed running back Rico Dowdle as questionable due to a knee injury and he is in danger of missing his first game since returning from a toe injury last week. The Steelers have also listed safety DeShon Elliott as questionable due to a knee injury while cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) and wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out. Of course, Kamara was limited in practice throughout the week as he continues to deal with a back injury, but he is off the injury report and will play against the Steelers. New Orleans has listed guard Cesar Ruiz as questionable due to a knee injury while defensive tackle Nathan Shepard is questionable with an illness. The Pittsburgh Steelers are in Paris Sunday morning as they face off against the New Orleans Saints in a Week 7 interconference matchup. Pittsburgh enters Sunday’s contest with a 4-2 record after defeating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road in overtime in Week 6. Aaron Rodgers led the way for the Steelers in their victory over the Buccaneers as he ended the game with 253 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and an interception while DK Metcalf recorded 93 receiving yards. The Steelers will try to grab another victory Sunday as they face off against the Saints in a tough matchup. New Orleans enters Sunday’s game with a 2-4 record after defeating the New York Giants on the road in Week 6. In their victory over the Giants, Tyler Shough led the way for the Saints as he recorded 176 total yards and four total touchdowns while Kendre Miller added 70 rushing yards. While both teams are looking to pick up a victory in Sunday morning’s matchup, each may be without multiple key players due to injuries. Steelers Injury Report: Will T.J. Watt, Rico Dowdle Play? The Steelers have four players listed on their injury report, though linebacker T.J. Watt is not one of them. If Dowdle is sidelined, Travis Homer could be in line for an increased role behind Jaylen Warren. Saints Injury Report: Will Alvin Kamara Play? The Saints have only two players listed on their injury report, though running back Alvin Kamara is not one of them. Fans can catch Sunday morning’s matchup between the Steelers and Saints from the Stade de France at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. home.blurb: The team was scheduled to have a walkthrough at Stade de France upon arrival, but those plans changed due to the weather and the team headed straight to their hotel, where they held media access and did not practice. McCarthy was asked during a Friday press conference if safety DeShon Elliott will be activated from the Reserve/Injured List. Elliot was a full participant all week and is listed as questionable. "He's a great player," said Benton. "He brought that vet mentality, and he was one of those guys that immediately you can ask him questions, and he'll have answers for you. Just those little tips and tricks to help out the younger guys, and myself included. Rubio has seen more playing time as of late and looks forward to continuing to contribute, even though he hates to see Joesph-Day out. "It's disappointing that he's down and out. But it's another opportunity for a next man up situation," said rookie Gabriel Rubio. "I said it a couple of weeks ago whenever I was elevated after (Derrick) Harmon's injury. So, we're going to see who's elevated to that spot. With receivers Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. both on the Reserve/Injured List, and Ben Skowronek already ruled out, the team will have to rely on a variety of options at the position. "Number one, it's great to see him," said McCarthy. "I had him as a youngster when he came out. So, I know he was here last year. You could just see when he walked in the building. Everybody was excited to have him back. McCarthy was asked if Valdes-Scantling would be available to play on Sunday if needed, but he wasn't ready to commit one way or another. Atlanta is searching for its first home win of the season, but San Francisco presents a major test for a team still trying to find consistency on both sides of the ball. Despite the 49ers dealing with injuries, the Falcons will need a complete performance to pull off the upset. Here is how our staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Garrett Chapman (3-3) The Falcons are winless at home this season, and they will need to pass a difficult test Sunday to change that trend. The undefeated 49ers have established themselves as one of the league’s top teams, and Atlanta enters the matchup with defensive holes to fill and an offense still searching for consistency. If Michael Penix Jr. can stay clean in the pocket, the Falcons will have a legitimate chance to compete. However, slowing down George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey will be especially difficult without linebacker Divine Deablo. San Francisco’s offensive weapons could prove too much for Atlanta’s defense, leading to another disappointing home result for the Falcons. Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 17 Scott Kennedy (3-3): At first glance, the betting line makes this matchup appear favorable for Atlanta. A 6-0 San Francisco team might be expected to be a bigger favorite, but the 49ers’ extensive injury concerns could be keeping the matchup closer than anticipated. The Falcons have enough talent to beat any team when they put everything together. The problem is finding that consistency against quality opponents. Atlanta must figure out how to handle opposing pressure, or the 49ers could overwhelm Penix with aggressive blitz packages. San Francisco is vulnerable because of its injuries, giving Atlanta a puncher’s chance. However, until the Falcons prove they can consistently perform against strong competition, picking them to pull off an upset remains difficult. Prediction : 49ers 31, Falcons 23 Darius Hayes (3-3): After Bears fans took over Mercedes-Benz Stadium last week, I expect another takeover from 49ers fans on Sunday. Atlanta should deliver a much better performance, but I still have concerns about whether the offense can do enough to secure a victory. San Francisco’s injuries will have an impact, but Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey will ultimately be too much for Atlanta’s defense. Meanwhile, the 49ers’ pass rush could make life difficult for Penix, particularly if the Falcons struggle to protect their young quarterback. I expect Atlanta to keep the game competitive and give its home crowd something to cheer about. However, until the Falcons demonstrate they can finish against a quality opponent, I cannot pick them to get over the hump. San Francisco escapes with a narrow victory, leaving Atlanta with another frustrating home loss. Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 24 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-3) The 49ers are currently the best team in football in my opinion which makes this a tough matchup for the Falcons. This would be a lopsided matchup if the 49ers were healthy, but that’s not the case. The 49ers have been led by arguably the best passing attack in the league, but they’ll be without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel . Stopping Georgie Kittle and McCaffrey will still be a tall order, however. The Falcons offense matches up well against the 49ers defense on paper, especially given that Nick Bosa will be out. The key will be can the Falcons o-line deal with all of the twists and stunts that the 49ers will throw at them, and can they keep Fred Warner from taking over the game. I have the 49ers winning, but I think the Falcons will keep it close. Prediction: 49ers 27, Falcons 20 Gerald Thomas, III (3-3) These are the kind of games the Falcons win. But after the last two weeks, it’s hard to pick them. This Atlanta team is still a work in progress, more than we assumed during the two-game winning streak, and the 49ers are a well-oiled machine. The skid continues. picks.blurb: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster. The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. The undefeated San Francisco 49ers pack their perfect record for a cross-country trip to face the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p. m. ET on FOX on Sunday, Oct. 25. My top 49ers vs. Falcons predictions and NFL picks recognize a brutal scheduling spot poses a real threat to the Niners, opening up prime value on star running back Bijan Robinson. 49ers vs Falcons prediction today: Falcons moneyline The market has moved significantly toward the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. The San Francisco 49ers opened as 4.5-point road favorites following their win over Washington on Monday. Early opinions have trimmed as many as two points off that spread, pushing through the key number of 3. If you read my Week 7 NFL Underdogs column, you know I grabbed Atlanta +3.5 earlier in the week. With the Falcons now trading at +2.5, I see more worth in their outright price rather than taking less than a field goal (underdogs of +2.5 or shorter are 12-13 SU and ATS this season). On top of injuries stacking up for the 49ers, specifically at receiver, this venture to Georgia is just San Francisco's second true road game of the season. Those home-friendly results produce a good chunk of the Niners' positive power ratings. This is also an early wake-up call for the 49ers, who take the field at 10 a.m. PT in Atlanta and do so on a short week , after playing on Monday in Week 6. There is also a looming look-ahead for a banged-up roster, with a bye waiting in Week 8. The Falcons are being downgraded for a sloppy loss to Chicago last weekend, in which Atlanta had three turnovers and less than 20 minutes of possession. Still, the Falcons were threatening in the fourth quarter. For a straight-up pick on every game, see our NFL moneyline picks for Week 7 . 49ers vs Falcons combo If you like a short underdog, often the moneyline is worth a wager. Atlanta stays home while the 49ers travel for an early kickoff on a short week. The chairman of tight ends has scored five touchdowns and sees his role in the passing game spike with the Niners potentially down their top two WRs. Bijan Robinson is an underrated pass-catching threat, and the Falcons need to get the ball in his hands by any means. Projections for Bijan flirt with as many as 40 receiving yards in Week 7. Falcons moneyline George Kittle touchdown Bijan Robinson 25+ receiving yards For more same-game parlays, see our NFL parlay and SGP picks . TOP PICK 49ers vs Falcons player prop: Bijan Robinson 25+ receiving yards The Falcons' path to victory is paved by running back Bijan Robinson . Robinson isn't just a threat to grind out gains on the ground, but also is a catch-and-run weapon in this offense. Robinson did finish with negative receiving yards on just two catches in the loss to Chicago last Sunday, which is helping slim his yardage total for Week 7 (had 30.5 O/U in Week 6). The game before, however, he was targeted seven times for four grabs and 32 receiving yards . Robinson is a workhorse for Atlanta and could see an even bigger snap share with fellow RB Brian Robinson Jr. dealing with a hamstring injury. Week 7 projections for Robinson's receiving output all sit north of 30 yards, with a ceiling of 39. My number comes out to 33+ receiving yards. For more NFL player props, see our NFL player prop projections . 49ers vs Falcons touchdown scorer: George Kittle Sunday is "National Tight Ends Day" in the NFL. While we're going to pay a TE tax on this annual appreciation, we can't deny George Kittle's role in this 49ers' offense in Week 7. Kittle, the unofficial founder of "TE Day", jumps up the pecking order in terms of targets. With WR1 Mike Evans hurting, Deebo Samuel out, and several other pass catchers on IR, Kittle could be busy. He has five touchdowns on the season, drawing 10 red-zone targets for eight catches and four TDs inside the 20-yard line. The Falcons have had their hands full versus rival TEs, giving up seventh most targets and receptions to the position, along with four touchdowns to tight ends. Kittle's touchdown forecasts are very positive, ranging from 53% to 61%. And for what it's worth, the Niners TE has struck paydirt in three of the last four "National Tight End Day" celebrations. Early 49ers vs Falcons spread pick: Falcons +3.5 The Atlanta Falcons didn't give themselves a fighting chance against Chicago last weekend. A series of miscues and turnovers kept Atlanta at arm's length, with the Falcons possessing the football for less than 20 minutes. They still managed to do damage with those limited possessions, finishing with the eighth-best points per play in Week 6. Atlanta suffered through some high-variance blunders, which is why I'm not writing it off against the spread in Week 7. The San Francisco 49ers are traveling on a short week for a 1 p.m. ET start time (10 a.m. PT) and have injuries on both sides of the ball. The Niners also have a much-needed bye waiting in Week 8, which could see San Fran play it safe with those ailing talents in an effort to give them extended rest. One other thing to note: the 49ers' hot start has come with the team playing only one true road game in the first six weeks due to starting the schedule "Down Under" in Week 1. away.headline: 49ers Injury Report: Kyle Shanahan says San Francisco may not have 48 available players against Falcons
away.blurb: 49ers injury report: Kyle Shanahan says San Francisco may not have enough available players to reach 48 for Week 7 vs. Falcons. Shanahan said he did not think he had ever faced a situation like this in his coaching career, calling it a unique situation. For a team trying to stay unbeaten on the trip to Atlanta, the concern is not just who will be unavailable, but whether the 49ers can even fill out a full game-day roster. Which players are out for Week 7? According to Shanahan, Mike Evans, Nick Bosa, Ricky Pearsall, Deebo Samuel Sr., De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Marques Sigle, Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford were unavailable or ruled out on Sunday. Christian Kirk was in line to make his season debut, but the overall health picture still left the roster in a difficult spot. The Bosa situation was particularly notable because Shanahan said the pass rusher had worked out after previously saying he might be able to return for Week 5 or Week 6. Shanahan said Bosa was a little sore the next day, which surprised the team and did not help the outlook for this week, especially with turf coming into play. Being short on available players is one thing. Being short enough to potentially miss the 48-man threshold is another. NFL teams can elevate players from the practice squad when injuries create depth problems, and that kind of move could become important for the 49ers if the injury list keeps growing. away.headline: 49ers Week 7 injury report vs. Falcons: Who will step up for SF with Mike Evans potentially out
away.blurb: Evans has been ruled out with Achilles, rib injuries He has been battling Achilles tendinitis this season. He left the Week 6 victory over the Commanders at halftime, and he has been ruled out of this game . In addition to the Achilles issue, Evans has a rib injury that is also impacting him. The hope for the 49ers is that he will be able to return in Week 9 when the Niners host the Las Vegas Raiders. Samuel is also out for the Niners Making matters worse for the 49ers is that fellow wideout Deebo Samuel will also miss the game. He is the team’s second-leading wide receiver, and he has a hamstring issue that is clearly impacting his ability to move on the football field. He was not able to participate in practice at any point this week and Shanahan also ruled him out of the game. McCaffrey is far more than a safety valve receiver out of the backfield. He can run multiple short, medium and long routes, and the Niners will likely use him out of the backfield in that fashion in this game. In addition to Evans and Samuel, edge rusher Nick Bosa has been ruled out with a calf injury. Other notable players who have been ruled out include starting S Marques Sigle with an ankle injury and depth LB Grant Wallow with a hamstring problem. This is not a must game for the 49ers. Their 6-0 record has given them a three-game lead over the Seattle Seahawks, and the most important thing for the Niners will be coming out of this game without any additional injuries. That may not be something they can control, but it is clearly something that could matter more than remaining undefeated at this point in the season. Related: 49ers’ Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel already ruled out for Falcons showdown The San Francisco 49ers have been brilliant to this point in the season and they have managed an undefeated record (6-0) as they prepare for their final game before the bye week. They are facing an inconsistent Atlanta Falcons team that is going to be determined to bounce back from a 31-23 defeat to the Chicago Bears. The circumstances of the game are also tough for the 49ers , because they are coming off a surprisingly tight 23-17 Monday night victory over the Washington Commanders, so that means they have are contending with a short week to prepare for a somewhat dangerous opponent. Head coach Kyle Shanahan will not concede anything in this game because he has one of the best quarterbacks in the game in Brock Purdy and he has been sensational to this point in the season. The same holds for running back Christian McCaffrey. Purdy has been on fire for the Niners It will be very difficult for the Falcons to slow either one down. Purdy is already in the discussion for the Most Valuable Player Award as he has completed 119 of 171 passes for 1,460 yards with 14 touchdown passes and 2 interceptions. The San Francisco offensive line has protected him quite well, as Purdy has been sacked just 5 times. McCaffrey may no longer be as quick or as explosive as he was during his peak years

home.headline: 49ers Injury Report: Kyle Shanahan says San Francisco may not have 48 available players against Falcons
home.blurb: 49ers injury report: Kyle Shanahan says San Francisco may not have enough available players to reach 48 for Week 7 vs. Falcons. Shanahan said he did not think he had ever faced a situation like this in his coaching career, calling it a unique situation. For a team trying to stay unbeaten on the trip to Atlanta, the concern is not just who will be unavailable, but whether the 49ers can even fill out a full game-day roster. Which players are out for Week 7? According to Shanahan, Mike Evans, Nick Bosa, Ricky Pearsall, Deebo Samuel Sr., De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Marques Sigle, Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford were unavailable or ruled out on Sunday. Christian Kirk was in line to make his season debut, but the overall health picture still left the roster in a difficult spot. The Bosa situation was particularly notable because Shanahan said the pass rusher had worked out after previously saying he might be able to return for Week 5 or Week 6. Shanahan said Bosa was a little sore the next day, which surprised the team and did not help the outlook for this week, especially with turf coming into play. Being short on available players is one thing. Being short enough to potentially miss the 48-man threshold is another. NFL teams can elevate players from the practice squad when injuries create depth problems, and that kind of move could become important for the 49ers if the injury list keeps growing. home.headline: 49ers Week 7 injury report vs. Falcons: Who will step up for SF with Mike Evans potentially out
home.blurb: Evans has been ruled out with Achilles, rib injuries He has been battling Achilles tendinitis this season. He left the Week 6 victory over the Commanders at halftime, and he has been ruled out of this game . In addition to the Achilles issue, Evans has a rib injury that is also impacting him. The hope for the 49ers is that he will be able to return in Week 9 when the Niners host the Las Vegas Raiders. Samuel is also out for the Niners Making matters worse for the 49ers is that fellow wideout Deebo Samuel will also miss the game. He is the team’s second-leading wide receiver, and he has a hamstring issue that is clearly impacting his ability to move on the football field. He was not able to participate in practice at any point this week and Shanahan also ruled him out of the game. McCaffrey is far more than a safety valve receiver out of the backfield. He can run multiple short, medium and long routes, and the Niners will likely use him out of the backfield in that fashion in this game. In addition to Evans and Samuel, edge rusher Nick Bosa has been ruled out with a calf injury. Other notable players who have been ruled out include starting S Marques Sigle with an ankle injury and depth LB Grant Wallow with a hamstring problem. This is not a must game for the 49ers. Their 6-0 record has given them a three-game lead over the Seattle Seahawks, and the most important thing for the Niners will be coming out of this game without any additional injuries. That may not be something they can control, but it is clearly something that could matter more than remaining undefeated at this point in the season. Related: 49ers’ Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel already ruled out for Falcons showdown The San Francisco 49ers have been brilliant to this point in the season and they have managed an undefeated record (6-0) as they prepare for their final game before the bye week. They are facing an inconsistent Atlanta Falcons team that is going to be determined to bounce back from a 31-23 defeat to the Chicago Bears. The circumstances of the game are also tough for the 49ers , because they are coming off a surprisingly tight 23-17 Monday night victory over the Washington Commanders, so that means they have are contending with a short week to prepare for a somewhat dangerous opponent. Head coach Kyle Shanahan will not concede anything in this game because he has one of the best quarterbacks in the game in Brock Purdy and he has been sensational to this point in the season. The same holds for running back Christian McCaffrey. Purdy has been on fire for the Niners It will be very difficult for the Falcons to slow either one down. Purdy is already in the discussion for the Most Valuable Player Award as he has completed 119 of 171 passes for 1,460 yards with 14 touchdown passes and 2 interceptions. The San Francisco offensive line has protected him quite well, as Purdy has been sacked just 5 times. McCaffrey may no longer be as quick or as explosive as he was during his peak years

away.headline: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return
away.blurb: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return Skip to main content SI.COM The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans came out. Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville. Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver. Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers. However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game. The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week. The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since. The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games. Michael Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Out Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game. Dillon Gabriel, Teven Jenkins, Out Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line. If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2. The Titans do not have much to offer on offense, but rookie Carnell Tate is having a solid season with 344 yards, which is only one yard behind Denzel Boston. Todd Monken believes that Ward will play with a finger injury, but advised, “We’ll see”. When Ward is on the field, quarterbacks generally do not even try to throw his way, but quarterback Cameron Ward can be reckless with the football and throw it his way, leading to a crucial turnover. It's a step forward for Winston, who has missed the past two games and did not practice leading up to the 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 18. The Titans designated linebacker Dorian Mausi (foot) to return, meaning he has a three-week window to practice but must remain on the injured reserve list. Titans safety Tony Adams (ankle) and receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) were both limited participants on Oct. 21. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers (rest) and running back Tyjae Spears (rest) did not practice.
