Things are turning from bad to worse for the Colts this season. After losing to the 0-5 Titans at home last weekend, the Colts fired their general manager and are looking to make some changes in the organization. A win on Sunday would go a long way in getting things going in the right direction again. You can find my best bet for this game in the Week 7 edition of the Road to 272 Bets. In this article, we're talking about player props. Let's dive into three of my favorites. Colts vs. Vikings Best NFL Prop Bets Odds via BetMGM Sportsbook Kyler Murray OVER 24.5 Rush Yards (-114) Jonathan Taylor UNDER 70.5 Rush Yards (-115) Aaron Jones Anytime Touchdown (+165) Kyler Murray looked much more like his former self in the Vikings' most recent game, rushing 10 times for 51 yards and using his legs significantly more than he had in his two games following his injury. I expect that to continue this week, especially with him having another week to rest during the Vikings' BYE. The Colts are 20th in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent rush success rate. No team stops the run more effectively than the Vikings, who rank first in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate. The Vikings also know that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, so I expect them to load up the box even more than normal and go all out in making sure that JT doesn't have a big game. It's also worth noting that the Colts' running back hasn't been as effective this season, averaging just 4.0 yards per carry, which is his lowest yards-per-carry average in his career. I'm surprised we can get such a good price on the Vikings running back to find the end zone this weekend. Not only have the Colts struggled to stop the run this season, but Jones has been fantastic when he's gotten the ball. He ran for 113 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries in the Vikings' final game before the BYE, so it's clear they don't mind handing him the ball early and often. With Shane Steichen on the hot seat following a rough 2-4 start, the Indianapolis Colts are teetering on the brink of a lost season as 6. 5-point road underdogs for Sunday's matchup against the unbeaten Minnesota Vikings. Fresh off a bye week and sitting atop an ultra-competitive NFC North with a 71% win probability in lines on Kalshi , my top Colts vs. Vikings predictions and NFL picks anticipate Minnesota's aggressive defense setting the tone for another comfortable home victory at U. TOP Pick Colts vs Vikings prediction today: Vikings -6.5 This ruthless Minnesota Vikings start is no fluke, as they've won 10 straight games dating back to last season, with an 8-2 ATS mark in that span , and their blitzing defense has Daniel Jones in its sights on Sunday. Brian Flores' aggressive unit ranks among the stingiest in the league against both the pass and the run (just 259.8 YPG allowed overall), and that spells trouble for an Indianapolis Colts team that's lost 11 of its past 13 contests and had three costly turnovers last weekend. Minnesota's bye week has also cleaned up the injury report, with T.J. Hockenson , Jordan Addison and Jordan Mason returning to diversify an offense that racked up 364 yards in Week 5 and capitalized on the defense's forced field position. Meanwhile, Indy is unlikely to have Sauce Gardner to throw at the Justin Jefferson assignment and could also be without key target Tyler Warren . Jones has already turned the ball over nine times through the first six games , and I'd bet this to 53%. For a spread pick on every game, see our NFL picks against the spread for Week 7 . Colts vs Vikings combo I expect a Minnesota win to come with a sharper offensive outing, with an extra week of preparation and more weapons for Kyler Murray to call on. The Vikings scored 39 points in their home opener against Green Bay, while the Colts gave up at least 30 points in road losses to Pittsburgh and Kansas City. The Over has been a winning ticket in Indy's last two contests, and this line feels too low for a matchup featuring Jefferson and (possible trade candidate) Jonathan Taylor on an indoor track. Jones' brief spell with the Vikings in 2024 at least means he knows what to expect here. Expect the Indy offense to lean heavily on Taylor and quick checkdowns. That's where Keenan Allen can thrive on Sunday, and he's been busy in his last three appearances, catching 19 of 29 targets for 190 yards . The Minnesota blitz will limit Jones' deep shots, but Allen's ability to win on short routes is highly valuable in this matchup. Vikings moneyline Keenan Allen Over 39.5 receiving yards Colts vs Vikings player prop: Kyler Murray Over 199.5 passing yards Murray's start with the Vikings has been bumpy, but he's found a rhythm with 225+ passing yards in back-to-back games. The ceiling is even higher here, with a healthier supporting cast for this Week 7 battle, and chunk plays are on offer against a banged-up Indy defense, especially with Addison's ability to stretch the field (average depth of target: 14.2 yards). Indoor conditions play to Murray's strengths, and he's gone past this number in his last eight home outings in Arizona and Minnesota (excluding the brief start in this year's season opener). However, they do not match up well with the Minnesota Vikings this Sunday. The Indianapolis Colts (2-4) will attempt to ground themselves on Sunday as they travel to Minneapolis to face the host Minnesota Vikings (5-0) before their season truly spirals out of control. The Colts' 2026 campaign is at a crossroads. After consecutive losses, including an embarrassing finish last week to the previously winless Tennessee Titans , the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard . Will that move spark the Colts and help them turn the tide, or will the team retreat into its shell? Trade rumors and thoughts of a slide are once again surrounding the Colts. This game could be a back-breaker unless they can avoid it. Here is how the ColtsRoundtable staff sees Sunday's game unfolding. Jake Arthur ( @JakeArthurNFL ): Vikings 23, Colts 13 "I'd often like to lead with the optimistic take on the matchup with a clear advantage the Colts have over their opponent, but I'm not sure there is one this week. Minnesota's defense blitzes far more than any other team, which is something the Colts' offense struggles against. The Colts can usually run the ball, but opponents are running against Minnesota less than anyone else because of the defensive fronts the Vikings present. The Vikings' offense isn't doing well despite having Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson, but they've had a week to figure out what to do, coming off their bye. "The Colts would often have the edge on special teams and penalties, but Minnesota's special teams are just as good as Indy's, if not better, and the Colts and Vikings are tied for being the second-least-penalized teams in the NFL. No Tyler Warren or Sauce Gardner for the Colts, and Minnesota doesn't have a soul on the injury report. The Vikings have the clear advantages in this one." Jake on the season: 2-4 Zach Hicks ( @ZachHicks2 ): Vikings 19, Colts 9 "The Colts limp into Minnesota coming off of their most embarrassing loss since 2024. They are without two of their best players in Warren and Gardner, while the 5-0 Vikings are looking healthy coming out of their bye week. "The Vikings boast the top defense in football, while the Colts' offense can't get out of their own way. This seems to be a recipe for disaster, with very little room for the Colts to make up this disadvantage. This should be an ugly kickers duel, with the Vikings coming out on top." Zach on the season: 4-2 The Colts take on the Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS .

picks.headline: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7
picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates J-Dub suffers devastating injury NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers Early Week 8 Waiver Wire Luka drops 52 on Jazz 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings enter their Week 7 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts looking to extend the league's longest winning streak. Since Week 14 of the 2025 season, the Vikings have won 10 straight games, building a 5-0 record going into last week's bye. They face a 2-4 Indianapolis team that fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen is still employed , but the Colts feel combustible right now, with rumors of trading away star players like RB Jonathan Taylor and G Quenton Nelson swirling. Minnesota can't afford to overlook Indianapolis if they want to keep pace with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. But this feels like an opportunity for the Vikings to jump on an inferior team that is going through organizational changes. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings when they host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday. Jordan Mason will run for 100+ yards and 2 touchdowns Jordan Mason appears to return to the lineup after missing the past four games with a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday that he expects to see Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw back at practice on Wednesday . With Mason back, Minnesota can return to its 1-2 punch with Aaron Jones. Indianapolis enters Week 7 as one of the league's worst run defenses. They rank 22nd in rushing yards allowed, but their 4.8 yards per run allowed is tied for 5th-worst in the league. Their 12.3% stuff-rate ranks 30th in the league, and they rank last in EPA/run allowed. I expect the Vikings to stay committed to the run game and give Jones some relief after he carried the ball 85 times for 370 yards from Weeks 2 to 5. Mason averaged 3.5 yards after contact per carry in 2025, tied for 11th-best in the league among qualifying running backs. I see him breaking 100 yards and reaching the end zone twice on Sunday. Jauan Jennings will catch a touchdown pass Trade rumors swirled around Jauan Jennings in the days after Minnesota's 23-13 win over the Saints in Week 5. He was caught on camera slamming his fist into the ground following Myles Price's fumble that was returned for a touchdown. That came two plays after Jennings appeared to get open for a potential touchdown, but Murray instead threw an incompletion to Tai Felton. One play later, Murray slightly overthrew Jennings in the end zone. Jennings has caught only two passes for nine yards this season, but the rumors of a potential trade seem to have died down. He's gotten open enough that he should be getting more targets, but look for him to find more separation downfield, with Justin Jefferson, Addison, and Hockenson potentially back this week. With extra attention on the other weapons on the field, Murray will make up for his red zone misses against the Saints. The Vikings will sack Daniel Jones 5+ times and pick him off multiple times This will be the first time Daniel Jones plays against the Vikings since spending the end of the 2024 season with them. He signed with the Colts last year and played well until a fractured fibula in Week 12 slowed him down, and an Achilles tear ended his season two weeks later. He completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards (8.1 yards per attempt), 19 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. Jones hasn't been as efficient this season, completing 59.6% of his passes and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt, with four touchdowns and six picks. He has been pressured on 42.1% of his dropbacks, tied for the league's 7th-highest mark. Of course, no one pressures quarterbacks as much as Minnesota does. They have a league-high 47.8% quarterback pressure rate, spearheaded by a 67.0% blitz rate that is 24.5 percentage points higher than the next-closest team. Look for the Vikings to get after Jones all day and force him into turnovers. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7

home.headline: Vikings get positive injury update on RB Aaron Jones: report
home.blurb: The veteran ball carrier exited the game in the fourth quarter as the Vikings posted 10 unanswered points to secure a 16-10 win over the visiting Colts. He was listed as questionable to return, but did not. Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones left Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts with a knee injury. Fortunately for the Vikings, this injury for Jones doesn’t appear to be serious. On Monday, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported a positive update on the Vikings RB. “Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as ‘day to day,'” Schefter reported. This injury for Jones occurred in the same game that fellow running back Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve. Mason missed each of the Vikings’ last four games after suffering a thumb injury in Week 1, forcing Jones to step up as the team’s bell-cow lead back. Mason led the Vikings in rushing on Sunday, taking 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones recording 26 yards on eight carries before exiting the game. The Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, boasting a 6-0 recording heading into this coming Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions. home.headline: Will Amon-Ra St. Brown, Ennis Rakestraw play for Lions vs Vikings?
home.blurb: "I think those guys’ll probably sit [out practice] Wednesday but the plan is to get them going Thursday," Campbell said. "I think they should be fine, they should be good. Now, we’ll see when we get there." [ NEW SHOW: Listen to the "Freep Sports Show" on our Detroit Free Press livestream on YouTube and available anywhere you listen to podcasts ( Apple or Spotify ). ] Rakestraw left midway through the fourth quarter after defending a short pass to Savion Williams and did not return. A second-round pick out of Missouri in 2024, Rakestraw has seen the most extensive action of his career this season after battling injuries early in his career , including a pulled hamstring as a rookie and a shoulder injury that required surgery last year. St. Brown caught nine passes for a season-high 153 yards against the Packers , but played just seven snaps in the fourth quarter because of his ankle injury. Rakestraw made his first start of the season Sunday, Oct. 25, in the Lions ' nickel package and played as part of a five-person rotation at cornerback along with Roger McCreary, D.J. Reed, Khalil Dorsey and Rock Ya-Sin. "It’s not major," Campbell said of Rakestraw's latest ailment. "He’s got a little ankle here. We feel like, as of right now, that he’ll be at practice Thursday. That’s kind of what we’re looking at, so – but we don’t feel like it’s major as of today." The Vikings (6-0) are the last remaining unbeaten team in the NFL, while the Lions are in third place in the NFC North at 4-2. Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs. Omar Cooper Jr.'s return adds another dimension after his 103-yard outing against New England. The other side of this matchup is just as concerning for Miami. I'll round out my combo with Smith, who I expect to thrive against a mediocre Dolphins pass defense. In 2025, the Dolphins swept the Jets, which included a 34-10 win at MetLife Stadium last December. Now the two divisional foes meet again in Week 7 in the Garden State. Here are our staff predictions for Jets vs. Dolphins at MetLife in Week 7: Bert Bainbridge The pick: Jets 27, Dolphins 20 Here's why: Before their Week 6 bye, the Dolphins have shown they're no push over with one-score losses against the Vikings and Bengals. Miami is able to keep it close again, but the Jets are able to hold on for the one-score victory in this divisional showdown at MetLife. Art Stapleton The pick: Jets 17, Dolphins 13 Here's why: The Dolphins are playing hard for North Jersey's Jeff Hafley, who is coming home as an NFL head coach for the first time. He's done a good job with an empty cupboard in terms of the roster. Expect the Jets to look to press the issue on defense and see if they can get Garrett Wilson going offensively. The pick: Jets 17, Dolphins 7 Here's why: The Dolphins aren't coming off a loss for the first time this season (they had a bye). Time for the Fish to get back to doing what they do best. The pick: Jets 20, Dolphins 14 Here's why: The Dolphins have been competitive during their last two games, but they're still 0-5. As long as the Jets don't get sloppy or turn the ball over, they'll win this game. Mike Dougherty The pick: Jets 21, Dolphins 17 Here's why: Yes, the Dolphins have been fiesty of late, but this is the week the league's seventh-best scoring defense has a profound impact on the outcome ... unless the Dolphins suddenly find a prolific running back. The pick: Jets 24, Dolphins 16 Here's why: While severely lacking in personnel, the Dolphins showed so far that they have enough fight to win at least a couple of games at some point this season. Will it be this week? The Jets should be able to hold up enough defensively to escape with a close win. Here's why: The Jets are the better team, albeit not by much. away.headline: There's Good News on the Injury Front for the Dolphins ... With a Big But
away.blurb: Both players were listed as limited participants, and there's absolutely no guarantee that either will be ready to go for the Week 7 game against the New York Jets. "He was a big bright spot early on," Hafley said. "Everybody was excited about him from training camp to preseason and the first couple games that he played. We were counting on him and then unfortunately he got injured. Monday he was out there, limited. Today he'll be out there and getting acclimated again. My expectations can't be too high because we've got to see him practice today. We've got to see how he feels tomorrow, kind of like Kyle. And then Friday to see what he's able to do and if he's able to go and help us out. But I am excited. I'm very excited. We've got two young players practicing that we're excited about, and we'll see what they can do today." The bottom line here is that having Douglas and Louis back will help when they're able to return, but maybe it won't happen this week, and if it does, maybe we shouldn't expect too much too soon from either of them. Douglas hasn't played since Week 2, while Louis has been out since sustaining a knee injury in the opener against the Las Vegas Raiders. Also back at practice Wednesday was edge defender Robert Beal Jr., who missed the past three games because of a hamstring injury. He also was listed as a limited participant in practice. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who continues to deal with a quad injury, was the only player on the 53-man roster who did not practice Wednesday. Along with Beal, Douglas and Louis, long-snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring) and running back Jaylen Wright (foot) all were listed as limited participants. home.headline: Jets' Aaron Glenn, Colts' Shane Steichen Hot Seat Status Revealed in Latest NFL Rumors
home.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . With the NFL season nearly halfway complete, a number of coaches are on hot-seat watch. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted that New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn could be one to watch in the coming weeks. "Nothing hard and fast right now as far as his tenure, from what I'm hearing after asking around," Fowler said (1:00 mark). "Look, Woody Johnson, the owner there, is really happy with Aaron Glenn as a whole as far as the progress they made in the offseason from Year 1 to Year 2... But that is a job to watch now, cause in Year 2, they're still struggling with some clock management issues." Amid the Indianapolis Colts' struggles, Fowler also pointed to Shane Steichen as another coach who could be on the hotseat. "Shane Steichen could be a lame duck situation at this point," Fowler said. "Now, they do value him. They want to give him a little bit of time. Talking to people around the league, they suspected that this window of time, dating back to the Minnesota game yesterday, the Jaguars game coming up and that next week before the trade deadline. If they can sort of get right and win at least one or two games, it could change their plan for their coaches and what they sell." This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

picks.blurb: Our Buccaneers vs. Panthers Score Predictions Are In Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Tampa Bay Buccaneers face a grim outlook for the rest of the season if they fall to 1-6 on the year. They can prevent that by defeating the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, but it won't be easy to win their first division matchup. The Bucs will have Baker Mayfield back in the fold after a three-game absence, but will that be enough to get a win? Our staff goes over our predictions for Sunday's matchup against the Panthers: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 21 It’s been tough sledding for the Bucs, but they might just have a chance to turn things around. Division play begins this week against the Panthers, and all signs point towards Baker Mayfield being back. While I do believe things will look better, I still think the offense is way off from being able to match Carolina’s offense, which will put up points. I think the Bucs will have a chance to win the game on the final drive, but ultimately fall short once again. James Hill, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 20 Mayfield's return is spoiled by the Panthers in this one. I simply think that Carolina is the better-coached team right now and that Mayfield may be slow to start back up after returning from his thumb injury. Collin Haalboom, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 17 The Buccaneers have played so poorly this season that they’re already on the verge of switching their primary focus from postseason contention to the top pick in next year’s NFL Draft. Considering we’re not even halfway through the season, I’d consider this season to be a full-scale nightmare for any Bucs fan. So, am I picking the Buccaneers to bounce back and take down the NFC South-leading Panthers in Carolina, you ask? No. I most certainly am not. Logan Robinson, Founder: Panthers 28, Bucs 23 The Panthers head into the game with the top passing attack in the league, and Bryce Young is playing at a high caliber. The Bucs and Todd Bowles have done a fair job of defending these types of offenses this season. My biggest concern is the offense for Tampa Bay. It’s quite obvious Zac Robinson’s offense doesn’t have an identity and even with Baker Mayfield coming back, I just don’t see it changing much. They’ll have to begin proving me wrong before I pick them to win games. Also, a reminder — the Cowboys are a bad football team. River Wells, Editor: Panthers 28, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay's defense will be tested by a Panthers offense that playcaller Brad Idzik has unlocked this season. Bryce Young is stretching the football down the field in a dominant way, so expect the Panthers to score points. Don't expect the Bucs to do much on offense in return. Zac Robinson's offense has been scattershot this whole season, and while Mayfield should play better than Jalon Daniels, he'll be playing with an injured thumb after a year where he didn't start off so hot anyway. Bucs have to be able to run the ball on Carolina — if they can't, they have no chance of winning. Consensus: Panthers 5, Bucs 0 The Buccaneers still haven't given us a reason to pick them to win a football game. They're 1-5 as it stands, and every BucsGameday staff member thinks they'll be 1-6 whenever they wake up in the morning. away.headline: Buccaneers expect Baker Mayfield back, rule out three starters
away.blurb: The Buccaneers' official Friday injury report lists wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out. Baker Mayfield remains questionable with a right thumb injury, although head coach Todd Bowles expects him to start against Carolina. Getting Mayfield back would significantly boost an offense that has struggled to establish consistency. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has done a respectable job given his limited NFL experience, but Mayfield's ability to recognize pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions gives offensive coordinator Zac Robinson more flexibility. However, Tampa Bay's offense will be far from full strength on Sunday. Egbuka missed Wednesday and Thursday's practices with concussion and foot injuries before returning Friday in a limited capacity. Despite the improvement, the team ruled him out for Sunday's game. His absence removes one of Tampa Bay's primary receiving threats from an offense that has already struggled to create consistent opportunities downfield. Goedeke also returned to practice in a limited capacity Friday after missing the previous two sessions with a calf injury. He was ultimately ruled out, leaving Tampa Bay without its starting right tackle. Protecting Mayfield will be especially important if he returns against a Carolina defense looking to exploit an offensive line that has struggled this season. Defensively, Winfield will miss Sunday's game with a rib injury. The veteran safety was limited all week but couldn't return to game action. His absence adds to the challenge for a young defense that has shown encouraging signs despite Tampa Bay's 1-5 record. Carolina will also deal with injuries, particularly on its defensive front. Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom were ruled out after missing all three practices. Offensive tackle Monroe Freeling and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott are questionable despite participating fully throughout the week. The Buccaneers enter Sunday's game looking to rebound from a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mayfield's expected return gives Tampa Bay reason to be optimistic, but the absences of Egbuka, Goedeke, and Winfield will force the team to adjust on both sides of the ball. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions for Bengals vs. Ravens in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates J-Dub suffers devastating injury NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers Early Week 8 Waiver Wire Luka drops 52 on Jazz 4 Bold Predictions for Bengals vs. Ravens in Week 7 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals are headed to Baltimore after the bye week. They currently sit at the bottom of the AFC North with a 3-2 record. The 4-2 Ravens are coming off a 13-10 loss to Cleveland. Joe Burrow did not mince words about avoiding a 0-2 division record: "We want to be 4-2 and controlling our own destiny." Baltimore has taken five of the last six meetings in this rivalry, including a 24-0 shutout last winter. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Dexter Lawrence Sacks the Quarterback Twice Cincinnati brought in All-Pro tackle Dexter Lawrence to make life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Lawrence shares the team sack lead with three, anchoring a defensive front that brings down passers on 10.12% of attempts. Baltimore's reshuffled offensive line gives him another opportunity to take over. Cam Jurgens is set to make his Ravens debut at center after recovering from a concussion, pushing Vega Ioane over to right guard. That leaves Jurgens with a difficult first assignment against Cincinnati's 340-pound anchor. Lawrence will dominate the A-gap, dropping Baltimore's signal-caller twice and collapsing the pocket before deep plays can develop. Tee Higgins Explodes for Over 100 Yards and Two Touchdowns Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5) and wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) celebrate a Higgins touchdown in the second quarter of the NFL Week 3 game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. The game was tied at 17 at halftime. Baltimore's secondary will have its hands full matching up on the perimeter. Ja'Marr Chase usually attracts plenty of attention from opposing defenses. That could leave Tee Higgins with more opportunities to exploit one-on-one coverage on the outside. Zac Taylor called Higgins a "major weapon" outside, pointing out that his past production against Baltimore often gets overlooked. Baltimore loves flooding the field with six defensive backs, but smaller defensive backs cannot match Higgins' massive frame . Burrow is going to test those 50-50 balls down the sideline, letting Higgins sprint his way to 100 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Jordan Battle Jumps a Route for Another Takeaway Jordan Battle is playing like a ball-hawking magnet right now. He shares the NFL lead with three interceptions after picking off two passes in Miami , and Taylor said this week that "turnovers scream at you" in division dogfights. Baltimore's passing attack has hit dead ends late in games, going scoreless in the second half three times. Backup Tyler Huntley averages just six yards a pop, while Lamar Jackson is working through a sore ankle. Battle will bait a throw over the middle, jump the passing lane, and flip the field with another huge takeaway. Boye Mafe and the Front Stop Derrick Henry Under 60 Yards Derrick Henry leads the league in rushing scores, but Cincinnati's rebuilt front is ready for the challenge. Taylor praised Mafe's work against the run earlier this week, saying that the defensive end's "willingness to set an edge and win in the run game is equally as critical as being able to rush the passer." Mafe and Cincinnati's front will swarm the boundary on early downs. By stacking the box and sealing outside lanes, Cincinnati will limit Henry to under 60 yards. away.headline: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7
away.blurb: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has not played since Week 4, and his status for Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals still remains unclear. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set as a 2.5-point favorite, though it remains -148 on the moneyline to win this game. It's not a major adjustment, but clearly there is some worry that Jackson could miss his third game in a row. Currently, DraftKings has received 73 percent of the moneyline bets in this game on the Bengals to win outright. After going down against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, Jackson has not played. He missed a win over Atlanta in Week 5 and a loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The Cleveland loss looms large for the Ravens, as they are now behind the Browns in the AFC North standings. The Ravens are a much more dangerous team with Jackson in the lineup, and he was an MVP candidate before going down in Week 4. This season, the star quarterback has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. A two-time MVP, Jackson leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Tyler Huntley would receive the start in Week 7 if Jackson can't go. away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens were completely dominated by the Cincinnati Bengals last game, as they lost by a 35-13 final score. Now, following their embarrassing Week 7 loss to the Bengals, the Ravens have added a new veteran defensive back to their depth. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Ravens have signed defensive back Rayshawn Jenkins to their practice squad. This comes after he was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers just a few days ago. Seeing the Ravens add a veteran like Jenkins to their practice squad is understandable. Their defense could use a boost, and Jenkins could provide them with that if he earns a spot on their active roster. Thus, there is no risk in Baltimore taking a look at a veteran like Jenkins for their practice squad. Jenkins appeared in six games this season with the Steelers before being released, where he posted 16 combined tackles. This is after he had 45 tackles in 17 games with the Cleveland Browns last season. In 145 career NFL games over 10 seasons, Jenkins has recorded 5.5 sacks and 578 combined tackles. The 29-year-old suffered the injury in Week 4 during the Ravens' game against the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. Ever since, Baltimore has struggled on the field in his absence, losing last week to the Cleveland Browns and narrowly escaping with a win in overtime against a shorthanded Atlanta Falcons team the Sunday before. Before the injury news came down, the matchup had been widely anticipated as the toughest test yet for Cincinnati's newly revamped defensive line, with Jackson named as the league MVP for the 2019 and 2023 seasons. home.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update Provided by Ravens HC amid Latest Rumors on QB's Timeline
home.blurb: Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter was optimistic about the quarterback's status even though he didn't know for sure whether the four-time Pro Bowler will be available for Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills. "Lamar's working his butt off to be back and be out there," Minter told reporters Monday. "I think he was able to get in a little bit of work obviously toward the end of last week. So I think he'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know a lot more on Wednesday." "The Ravens are hopeful he'll be back this week, but the truth of the matter is, only Lamar Jackson knows when he'll be back," Schefter said. "He returned to practice last week in a limited fashion, but just like he missed three games last year at this time with a hamstring injury, he's now missed three games in October with a high-ankle sprain. … But I think everybody's hopeful he can be back in time for Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills." It likely needs Jackson back and at his best if it is going to be a serious factor in the AFC playoff race, and it seems like his return will be sooner rather than later even if there is still some remaining uncertainty. ESPN's Adam Schefter also reported on the situation and stressed the team is "hopeful" its leader will be on the field for such a highly anticipated AFC showdown. Jackson's exact status has been something of a question mark, as he practiced some before Baltimore's game against the Cincinnati Bengals but didn't take the field. Minter was asked about the overall messaging surrounding the injury since he previously called Jackson "day-to-day" while the quarterback said it was a high ankle sprain that prevented him from running. "When the player is healthy enough to play, they'll play," Minter said while also reiterating the team will know more Wednesday. "… There's things that change sometimes with injuries and what you think of it right when it happens in a game where the adrenaline and things are still going on." Tyler Huntley has played for Jackson during the starter's absence and led the team to a victory over the Atlanta Falcons before losing to the Cleveland Browns and Bengals in AFC North games. Baltimore is now 4-3 overall but 0-2 in the division and in last place.

home.headline: Report: Ravens to sign veteran safety Rayshawn Jenkins
home.blurb: The Ravens are adding experience to a secondary that struggled to contain Cincinnati during Sunday’s second-half collapse. NFL insider Jordan Schultz says Baltimore is signing veteran safety Rayshawn Jenkins. The move gives the Ravens another option in the defensive backfield after a 35-13 loss to the Bengals dropped them to 4-3. Pittsburgh released Jenkins on Oct. 21. The 10-year veteran appeared in six games for the Steelers this season, made one start, and recorded 15 tackles. Pittsburgh’s release announcement credited him with 145 career appearances, 93 starts, and 11 interceptions. Baltimore needs depth immediately with starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins sidelined by a knee injury. Hawkins missed Sunday’s game, though coach Jesse Minter said the injury wasn't considered a long-term concern. The urgency increased against Cincinnati. Joe Burrow completed 16 of 18 second-half passes for 249 yards and four touchdowns as the Bengals scored 35 unanswered points. Baltimore used K’Von Wallace and Keondre Jackson at safety in Hawkins’ absence. Jenkins brings extensive starting experience, but his role will depend on how quickly he learns the defense and how Baltimore’s injured players progress. As the team prepares to visit Buffalo, the reported addition gives the Ravens another option as they work to stabilize their pass defense. The Ravens announced the signing of veteran safety Rayshawn Jenkins to the practice squad, adding depth to a secondary dealing with injuries. picks.headline: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New York Giants might have a winning record (3-2-1) right now and lead the NFC East. But let’s be honest. Aside from their dominant Week 1 showing against the Dallas Cowboys, have the Giants really looked as good as their record suggests? We’re talking about a team where the phrase “A win’s a win” applies. The Giants barely beat the Tennessee Titans, 12-7, in Week 3. They also had to fight back in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, who led 24-19 at one point. The tie against the Commanders? That one was a gift. If Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn don’t have that brain blip, the Commanders likely win, despite the Giants roaring back from a 19-6 deficit. And last week? We’re sorry, but the Giants had no business losing to the New Orleans Saints as badly as they did. And again, make no mistake: the Giants lost that game because they were their own worst enemy, as shown by the sloppy play they put on film. But it’s funny how the football gods work. The Giants, regardless of what they do against the Houston Texans this week, will remain in first place in the division. They have a chance, albeit a difficult one, to get back to looking like the team they were in Week 1, even though they’ve since lost a lot of key personnel, all of whom played in that win: quarterback Jaxson Dart, returner/receiver Braxton Berrios, outside linebacker Brian Burns, and inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds. So what’s the goal this week if the Giants want to pull off an upset win over the Texans on the road? “We’ve been practicing well the last few weeks,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “I think practice has been improving every single week, which is the mark of a team that has got a chance to do something. You’ve got to keep improving. “So, we are on track to do that. I’m looking forward to it showing up in terms of consistency. If we’ve been anything, we’ve been inconsistent.” It’s really that simple. The question is, will the Giants finally find the consistency that’s eluded them since that Week 1 game? Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans The Texans might be on a roll, having won their last two games, but they still have a few flaws that could work to the Giants’ advantage. For one, the Texans’ offensive line ranks 27th in the PFF pass-blocking efficiency rating metric. The unit has allowed 71 quarterback pressures, tied for third-most in the league. Left tackle Aireontae Ersery has allowed 20 quarterback pressures, per PFF, tied for fourth-most in the league among left tackles. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has turned up the heat on opposing quarterbacks in recent weeks. This year, opposing quarterbacks have completed only 54.1% of their pass attempts against the Giants’ blitz, the fourth-lowest completion rate in the league. Of course, the key is for the Giants to stop the run, something they haven’t done consistently in recent weeks. So we’ll see if Wilson’s calling out his defensive players for not running to the ball lights a fire underneath them. Offensively, the Giants need to get their running game going, and the hope is that switching to quarterback J.J. McCarthy will help. This more mobile quarterback will discourage the Texans from loading up the box and start accounting for McCarthy as a runner. More importantly, McCarthy’s ability to scramble away from trouble could help the Giants’ ailing offensive tackles, Andrew Thomas and, if he plays, Jermaine Eluemunor, against that Texans pass rush. Per Next Gen Stats, since 2025, McCarthy has scrambled 19 times for 185 yards and three touchdowns, a 9.7 yards-per-carry average, which is a league high among quarterbacks with a minimum of 15 carries. If McCarthy can buy time, he stands a chance at connecting with receiver Malik Nabers or tight end Isaiah Likely, both of whom have been the most frequently targeted players on offense for the Giants over the last few weeks. Why the Giants Will Lose to the Texans I touched on it a bit above, but I’ll say it again here. The Giants have to stop the run. Texans’ top running back, David Montgomery, has been sidelined with a groin injury, but Woody Marks has stepped up in his place. Marks is an explosive running back who has averaged almost four yards per rush over the last two weeks. He also has six catches for 47 yards over that span. The Giants’ run defense? Not good at all. Big Blue has allowed opponents 135.5 rushing yards per game this year, and their 5.0 yards per carry allowed is the second-worst average in the league. If the Giants can’t stuff Marks and the Texans’ running game, it won’t matter what pass-rush plan they have this week. And until the unit shows it has cleaned up the missed tackles (13 last week, seven against the run per PFF), that aspect of the game will remain the team’s Achilles heel. At the start of the season, I had this game down as a loss and nothing — not even the Texans’ 2-4 record or the Giants’ 3-2-1 start — has changed my mind. The Texans have been coming into their own lately, and the Giants, aside from their Week 1 win over Dallas, have barely gotten by in their other wins and in their tie against Washington. The Giants will fight — that much I am certain of — and I hope this doesn’t turn into the ugly rout that I fear it could become. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. Stroud (7) celebrates his touchdown with wide receiver Nico Collins (12) against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. away.headline: Giants’ Cam Skattebo injury update brings heavy sigh of relief after OT scare
away.blurb: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo made a significant impact in the team’s Week 7 overtime win over the Houston Texans with an impressive 42-yard run. However, he wisely slid to the ground at the 30-yard line after feeling a twinge in his hamstring, avoiding being caught from behind. Following the thrilling win, there was immediate concern regarding his injury, but those worries were quickly alleviated. According to a report shared on X by Mike Garafolo, Skattebo informed Dan Graziano that he experienced some discomfort in his hamstring during that 42-yard run. Fortunately, all indications the following morning suggested that he would be fine, especially with the team having a bye week this weekend. This is a rare and welcome situation for the Giants, as it means they won’t face any injury-reserve candidates after the game. The upcoming bye week provides Skattebo, a dynamic player, with ample recovery time without having to miss any game action. Despite his health being intact, Skattebo had much to say after the game about a controversial 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty he received for lowering his helmet against M.J. Stewart. He criticized what he perceives as a double standard in the league, where his physical running style is praised but then penalized. A fired-up Skattebo vowed to maintain his aggressive playing style, remarking that if the fines continue to accumulate, he might as well just “play for free.” Like ClutchPoints’ content? away.blurb: The extra rest should allow Skattebo to return healthy to the backfield as New York aims to maintain its divisional edge. News Sports Business Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals GIANTS Report: New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo avoided major injury Dan Benton Giants Wire Oct. 26, 2026, 10:50 a.m. ET New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo should avoid significant injury after feeling something in his hamstring on a 42-yard overtime run that helped secure a 27-21 victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported on Monday that all indications are the second-year back should be OK, a rare positive for a Giants team that often has injured reserve (IR) candidates after games, particularly with a bye this weekend. After the Week 7 win, Skattebo told ESPN’s Dan Graziano he did not intend to slide on the play that set up Devin Singletary’s game-winning 30-yard touchdown. He felt something in his hamstring and knew the Giants were in field-goal range, so he went down at the Houston 30. He noted the bye week’s timing was fortunate. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reported that Skattebo avoided straining the muscle. The carry was the longest of Skattebo’s career and highlighted a bounce-back outing in which he rushed 17 times for a career-high 124 yards and a touchdown. It followed a week in which he received zero carries against the New Orleans Saints after an overtime fumble versus the Washington Commanders in Week 5. The Giants improved to 4-2-1, leading the NFC East, and will have the bye before traveling to Philadelphia on November 8. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL J-Dub suffers devastating injury New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

He admitted that "without a doubt" it isn't easy to no longer have a starting role. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Broncos -4.5 (-110) Cardinals +4.5 (-110) Broncos: -230 Cardinals: +190 43.5 (Over -115/Under -105) This line has held steady since it opened , as the Broncos are still favored on the road by 4.5 points despite Arizona’s win over the Rams in Week 6. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.headline: Pat Surtain injury: Latest updates for Broncos cornerback
away.blurb: Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain went down with a non-contact ankle injury late in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers . He was ruled out in the third quarter. After sitting out Sunday's game, Pat Surtain told the Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson that he wasn't really close to playing in Week 7. When asked if he could return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, Surtain said, "Possibly." Broncos CB Pat Surtain is inactive and will miss his third straight game. However, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport tweeted on Sunday that " there's a good chance " Surtain will be able to return against the Chiefs in Week 8. Broncos CB Pat Surtain questionable for Week 7 Denver's injury report for Sunday's game against Arizona has cornerback Pat Surtain officially listed as questionable . If he can't play, Jahdae Barron will likely be the next man up. Despite returning to practice on Wednesday, Pat Surtain seems more likely to return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, according to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video . We'll see how the week goes for PS2. Pat Surtain might not return in Week 7 In an updated report on Pat Surtain's status, James Palmer of Prime Video clarified that PS2's injury was not a non-contact injury — it actually happened one play before the cornerback went down on the field. Palmer also reported that " [i]t might be tough " for Surtain to return to action in Week 7, suggesting PS2 might be more likely to return in Week 8. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported this morning that Pat Surtain is expected to miss time, but it's not believed to be season-ending. "You hope it is just a couple weeks, maybe it ends up in an IR stint, but not expected to be season-ending," Rapoport said . If Surtain is placed on injured reserve, he would have to sit out at least four games. Broncos CB Pat Surtain ruled out Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), who were both originally listed as questionable to return, have been announced as ruled out for the rest of today's game. Riley Moss and Jahdae Barron are the two outside cornerbacks with Ja'Quan McMillian playing in the slot. Behind them on Denver's depth chart , the Broncos also have Kris Abrams-Draine. With PS2 sidelined, the team is down to four healthy cornerbacks on the active roster. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. Denver previously elevated two cornerbacks from its practice squad after injuries sidelined Surtain and fellow starter Riley Moss. Moss, who suffered a rib injury against San Francisco, returned against Seattle and played 20 defensive snaps. He practiced fully throughout this week and carries no injury designation for Sunday's game, giving Denver an important boost even if Surtain remains sidelined. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have also taken on larger responsibilities in the secondary, while Ja'Quan McMillian has continued handling the slot cornerback position. Denver's defensive depth remains under pressure elsewhere. The Broncos enter Sunday's matchup at 4-2 after consecutive victories, while the Cardinals are 2-4.
