The Packers, winners of three in a row, are coming off a 23-13 defeat of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Meanwhile, Detroit, which spent Week 6 on its bye, defeated the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, 45-21. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 7 matchup with Green Bay. Christian Booher The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness. Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose. Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win. While the Lions have the ability to keep up in the event this game becomes a shootout, the Packers are uniquely equipped to attack the Lions' issues in coverage, both in the secondary and at linebacker. Green Bay makes one more play than Detroit, and hands Dan Campbell's team a crushing loss to start a crucial two-game stretch. Packers 31, Lions 28 The Detroit Lions have a big time test ahead of themselves on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers not only are red hot and winners of three in a row. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs. In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers. Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair. Yet, the Lions' defense will be in the best shape it's been all season due to the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch. He should provide a major boost to the team's secondary and put it in a stronger position to limit the productivity of Watson and Golden. I think Detroit's pass defense holds up just enough and Jared Goff and the offense come through in the fourth quarter, leading Dan Campbell's squad to its fourth victory of the season. Lions 31, Packers 24 John Maakaron The Lions return to action after a much needed week off. The Packers are visiting Ford Field missing a few key players, but will have running back Josh Jacobs in the lineup. If the defensive line can have another strong performance, Jordan Love will not have ample time to find his key targets. Tight end Tucker Kraft could be in line for a big game, but Detroit’s offense should keep the momentum from the first quarter of the season rolling. Sam LaPorta might just also have himself a productive afternoon, given the noise he created and wanting to prove he deserves a lucrative new contract. Emmett Matasovsky The Lions start divisional play with the Green Bay Packers this week, and it sees the return of Brian Branch and Josh Jacobs for their respective teams. That makes this week even more intriguing. It will be interesting to see how, or if, the bye week has given Detroit time to somewhat fix its porous secondary. The return of Branch will give fans a glimpse as to how this secondary should operate, but the boundary corner issues could make this discussion irrelevant. Green Bay is a hard team to gauge, even before factoring in the wild card element that it is a divisional game in the NFC North. The Lions, on fresh legs and with momentum, alongside a rowdy Ford Field crowd, take the win to open the second half of the season. picks.blurb: Packers-Lions Prediction: Will Green Bay Beat Odds So It Can Beat Rivals? The Packers are coming off a Sunday night home game. The Lions are coming off a Sunday at their homes with their bye week. So, Detroit – in a huge NFC North game, mind you, that could have playoff ramifications – has been given by the league a home game and a week of rest. Will it matter? Here are our predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Lions Prediction Since the start of the 2020 season, teams with a home game after their bye are 63-41, according to Stathead. That’s an enormous advantage. Will that alone decide the game? Probably not. But in a game between two quality teams – the Lions are 3.5-point favorites – it might not take much to be the tipping point. Eight consecutive games at Ford Field between the teams ended with a one-score differential; the last exception was in 2017, when Brett Hundley was the Packers’ quarterback. Both teams are going to score points. A lot of points. The over/under of 55.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel. The Lions on offense have been a well-oiled machine. It tallied 30 points in five of six games this season and is second in the league in scoring. Quarterback Jared Goff hasn’t thrown an interception all season. He is surrounded by probably the best quartet in the league with receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta. Green Bay’s defense was great last week against the Dak Prescott-led Cowboys passing attack, but it didn’t have to contend with a back like Gibbs, who is arguably the best in the league – especially at home. The Packers have been hit and miss on offense – which is about what you’d expect for a team with a big-time quarterback and two big-play receivers but with an inconsistent offensive line and an unimaginably bad running game. The matchup is favorable, though, because the Lions’ defense has been terrible. It ranks 30th in points allowed and 32nd in total defense. At its current clip, it will threaten the 2011 Packers as the worst pass defense in NFL history. For the Lions, the best defense has been a good offense. They are 3-2 despite allowing 20 touchdowns. According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, they are the first team in NFL history to allow 20 offensive touchdowns and have a winning record through five games. Ultimately, three big issues stand the Packers’ way. One, they have struggled to protect Love. Well, the Lions lead the NFL in sacks even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Can Green Bay’s tackles overcome the noise to keep Aidan Hutchinson away from Love? Two, they have struggled to pressure the quarterback at times. Goff is an elite quarterback when given time. As coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “It’s hard for a quarterback to throw when he’s on his back.” Can the Packers put Goff on his back enough? Furthermore, the Green Bay defense will line up without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. And, finally, there’s this festering problem: The Packers have fatal flaws they haven’t solved. Love has been stymied by 19 drops; no other quarterback has more than 11. They lead the league in penalties and penalty yards. Love has faced the third-most pressures. “The simple stuff, whether from scheme-wise or the understanding of what we’re trying to get done, when you have some mistakes that can lead to negative plays, that’s the stuff we got to clean up and be better at,” Love said. It’s those things that will put the Packers at a disadvantage in every big game – no matter the location or scheduling quirk – until they get them fixed. Ultimately, the team that makes the fewest mistakes will win. Based on the first five games, it’s hard to believe that will be the Packers. Bill Huber’s Prediction: Lions 31, Packers 27. Bill’s Record: 3-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Lions Prediction The Packers have lost too many games like these in recent years, which have caused them to travel the long road in the postseason. In 2024, they lost all but one division game, which played a significant factor in them being the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. Last year’s late-season debacle in Chicago essentially sealed their fate that the wild-card meeting rematch would be at Soldier Field instead of the friendly confines of Lambeau Field. Simply put, the Packers need to knock off the Lions on the road on Sunday to keep pace with those in front of them and remain in position to be a legitimate NFC North contender. In a game where points should be scored in bunches, one mistake could be the difference. Who do you trust more to play clean and disciplined? Dan Campbell's Lions or Matt LaFleur's Packers? That, combined with the Lions being at home off a bye, gives them the nod. Jacob’s Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 31 Jacob’s Record: 3-3. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. away.blurb: Packers get bad news as update on center Sean Rhyan reveals multi-week injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services Apple TV Add Sporting News on Google div))]:my-4" data-testid="advert--mobile_branded_logo" id="Branded_Logo_Mobile"> The Green Bay Packers have had a lot of issues in the running game this season, but Josh Jacobs is back, meaning their time running the ball should be easier. However, the Packers aren't going to be operating with a fully healthy offensive line going forward this season. It's been a banged-up unit this year already, and now, the Packers are losing another key starter. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Packers got some bad news on center Sean Rhyan, who is now set to miss multiple weeks as he deals with a high ankle sprain. Packers get bad news on Sean Rhyan amid high ankle sprain injury "Packers C Sean Rhyan, who left Sunday's game with an ankle injury, is believed to have suffered a high-ankle sprain, sources say," Rapoport reports. "X-Rays were negative, and he has an MRI today. But high-ankle sprains are often 4-6 week injuries." The Packers have already been dealing with some backups along the offensive line this season, and now, coming off a heartbreaking Week 7 loss to the Detroit Lions , they just lost another key lineman. Now at 4-3, the Packers will be without Rhyan for multiple weeks, with this injury potentially one that lands him on injured reserve. MORE : Why Lions' Sam Laporta contract situation 'more likely than not' has a good ending With multiple other offensive linemen hurt, the Packers need to find a fix up front, especially with the short week coming up. In Week 8, the Packers will have to find a new center to play on Thursday Night Football against the Carolina Panthers . While the Panthers' defense isn't one to fear, this Packers team will need to fix this center problem in just a couple of days. away.headline: Matthew Golden injury update & more from Packers’ Monday practice report
away.blurb: We did see Golden get shaken up briefly on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, but he only left for one play. In fact, he would have stayed on the field if he wasn’t forced to sit out for the snap. This now leaves Golden’s status at least somewhat up in the air just three days out from the Thursday night contest between Green Bay and Carolina. On the bright side, guard Aaron Banks was estimated as limited, and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste was a full participant. The news isn’t as good for Rhyan, who is believed to have suffered a high-ankle sprain that could keep him out a month or more, Rapoport reported . The Packers will release two more injury reports, one on Tuesday and another on Wednesday, before they hand out designations on the latter day. The Green Bay Packers have dropped their first injury report of the week ahead of the Week 8 game against the Carolina Panthers and wide receiver Matthew Golden is on it. The injury report was an estimation , but it has Golden listed as a non-participant. This marks the second straight week Golden has been on the injury report. However, this time around, Golden has a new issue, with a foot being added to the shoulder injury he was on the injury report with last week. Along with Golden, defensive tackle Anthony Campbell, linebacker Zaire Franklin, offensive lineman Travis Glover, center Sean Rhyan and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt were all estimated non-participants. It was revealed on Monday morning that Franklin, who missed last week’s game after getting accidentally kicked in practice, is dealing with a hairline fracture in his leg, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport . The good news is, he is not expected to be placed on injured reserve and may only miss “minimal games,” Rapoport said.

away.headline: Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs contrite as he prepares to play again amid ongoing NFL investigation

home.headline: Will Amon-Ra St. Brown, Ennis Rakestraw play for Lions vs Vikings?
home.blurb: "I think those guys’ll probably sit [out practice] Wednesday but the plan is to get them going Thursday," Campbell said. "I think they should be fine, they should be good. Now, we’ll see when we get there." [ NEW SHOW: Listen to the "Freep Sports Show" on our Detroit Free Press livestream on YouTube and available anywhere you listen to podcasts ( Apple or Spotify ). ] Rakestraw left midway through the fourth quarter after defending a short pass to Savion Williams and did not return. A second-round pick out of Missouri in 2024, Rakestraw has seen the most extensive action of his career this season after battling injuries early in his career , including a pulled hamstring as a rookie and a shoulder injury that required surgery last year. St. Brown caught nine passes for a season-high 153 yards against the Packers , but played just seven snaps in the fourth quarter because of his ankle injury. Rakestraw made his first start of the season Sunday, Oct. 25, in the Lions ' nickel package and played as part of a five-person rotation at cornerback along with Roger McCreary, D.J. Reed, Khalil Dorsey and Rock Ya-Sin. "It’s not major," Campbell said of Rakestraw's latest ailment. "He’s got a little ankle here. We feel like, as of right now, that he’ll be at practice Thursday. That’s kind of what we’re looking at, so – but we don’t feel like it’s major as of today." home.headline: Detroit Lions injury updates: Dan Campbell shares Monday report
home.blurb: Detroit saw cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. exit with an ankle injury . Star receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown also had an ankle that got checked out on Sunday. The Detroit Lions (4-2) are readying for a showdown this weekend against the NFL's lone remaining unbeaten in the Minnesota Vikings (6-0). Campbell was optimistic about that duo's statuses for the remainder of this week and then heading into Sunday's matchup against the Vikings . "Yeah, I think (Amon-Ra) and Ennis will probably sit Wednesday, but the plan is to get them going Thursday, and I think they'll be fine. They should be good. Now, we'll see when we get there," Campbell said. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs wisely got down inside the Packers ' 5-yard line after converting a 3rd-and-6. That decision from Gibbs allowed Jake Bates to hit a 22-yard field goal as time expired, eliminating any chance for Jordan Love and the Packers to drive the field or connect on a Hail Mary. But, Gibbs went down awkwardly. Fortunately, Campbell said on Sunday night that everything was good with Gibbs. "Yeah, we got him checked. He should be good. That's that whole is it really worth going down to try to finish the game, or you just go score? Sometimes I question that. I don't know. Maybe we should have just (scored). But, all good. It's a good win," Campbell said. Gibbs finished with 116 rushing yards on 29 carries. St. Brown was the Lions' leading receiver, catching nine passes for 153 yards in the win over the Packers. Kickoff on Sunday is set for 1 p.m. ET between the Lions and Vikings from Ford Field. For more Lions coverage, follow us on X, @TheLionsWire , and give our Facebook page a like . picks.blurb: Raiders vs. Rams Week 7 expert picks and predictions for Sunday's game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates J-Dub suffers devastating injury NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers Early Week 8 Waiver Wire Luka drops 52 on Jazz Raiders vs. Rams Week 7 expert picks and predictions for Sunday's game Marvin Uzor, Raiders Wire Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:50 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Last week, Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr was nearly the sole holdout in picking the Raiders to edge past the Buffalo Bills . Well, anyone backing the Raiders in Week 7 has a lot more company, with a good chunk of the experts giving them a real shot against the Rams Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Covering the spread against Buffalo apparently buys a team some respect. The computer models still like the Rams comfortably, but some of the humans are far less sure, and a few of them switched sides from last week. Even the Raiders Wire staff is on board too, picking the Raiders 3-1 with an average score of 27-25. NFL.com's panel can barely agree Three of NFL.com's five analysts picked the Rams, with Jeremy Bergman at 24-17, Gennaro Filice at 27-24 and Dan Parr at 31-27. The other two went with the Raiders, and both picks come with a story. Bobby Kownack had the Bills hanging 35 points on the Raiders last week. Now he has the Raiders winning a 17-14 rock fight , which is quite a change of heart in seven days. Brooke Cersosimo has the Raiders by one at 25-24, and the Rams clearly gave her more to think about than she expected. "Of all the teams in the league, I would not have guessed the Rams would give me pause at this point in the season," Cersosimo wrote. She also has the game ending on a Raiders field goal in the final minute. Bleacher Report's experts traded seats The funniest twist came from Bleacher Report. Maurice Moton was the panel's lone Raiders backer last week, and this week he jumped to the Rams, while Gary Davenport, who doubted the Raiders against Buffalo, came over to their side. "Why lay this many points on the road against a Raiders team that just covered the same spread against Buffalo?" Davenport wrote. Moton expects the Rams to adjust without Davante Adams by leaning on their tight ends. The panel finished 4-3 in favor of the Raiders against a 4.5-point spread, with Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski joining Davenport. Pete Prisco and Mike Florio keep it tight CBS Sports' Pete Prisco picked the Rams to win by a single point, 28-27, which is a polite way of taking the Raiders against the spread. "They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here," Prisco wrote. "But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders, who hang around." The rest of the CBS panel split 4-3 for the Rams against the spread, with Tyler Sullivan and Jamey Eisenberg standing with Prisco. Meanwhile, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has the Rams winning 26-23 and sees a season on the line for Los Angeles. "If the Rams get to five losses with 10 games left, they could be done," Florio wrote. The computers aren't buying it The models are far more confident than we (humans). Dimers gives the Rams a 70.8% chance to win with a 26-20 projection, and the Covers AI model has Los Angeles winning 27-20. Five of the seven human score predictions in this roundup land within three points, though. These experts expect another one-score game, and the Raiders have lost two of their last three games by a field goal. But the Rams potentially adding wide receiver help shouldn't come as a huge surprise, as they had already been one of the teams linked to WRs on the trade market, even before the Adams injury. This is an all-in team after their blockbuster trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie. Spending a few more draft picks on WR help wouldn't be a surprise whatsoever. They've already mortgaged their future on this 2026 roster. Graziano is reporting that WR help is something Les Snead and Sean McVay will consider adding. While the 2-4 Rams might not seem like a buyer, this team is in too deep to not continue striving for a title in 2026. home.headline: Las Vegas Raiders Get Big Injury News on Monday
home.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders received a timely boost on Monday when they designated second-year wide receiver Jack Bech to return to practice from the Reserve/Injured list, the team announced . The move opens a 21-day window for the team to evaluate whether the former second-round pick is ready to rejoin the active roster or must return to injured reserve for the remainder of the season. The offense has shown competence at times, yet the lack of consistent production from anyone other than Tucker has limited the unit’s ceiling, particularly as the defense has struggled. A return as soon as Week 8 against the New York Jets appears unlikely given the timing of the designation. Kubiak has emphasized that Thornton still needs to prove he is ready, leaving his status uncertain even as Bech begins the return process. With the season still within reach of a playoff push if the Raiders can reverse their recent form, the return of a young wideout with early production offers a modest but concrete path toward more balanced offensive production. Whether Bech can immediately carve out a role or needs additional time to regain timing will become clearer over the next two weeks of practice. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing Bech had been sidelined since late September after fracturing his forearm during the Raiders’ Week 3 victory over the New Orleans Saints. Before the injury, Bech had recorded five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown on six targets while operating as the No. 3 option behind Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor. His absence left the receiving corps thinner than hoped in a season that began with three straight wins but has since slipped to 3-4. Bringing Bech back into the building gives coaches a chance to see if the 2025 draftee can provide the additional playmaking the team has sought. A more realistic target is the following week against the San Francisco 49ers, assuming Bech progresses cleanly through practice and shows he can handle the physical demands of an NFL game. The Raiders would not have opened the practice window if they did not believe he was reasonably close to contributing. The same roster decisions loom for another young receiver. Dont’e Thornton Jr., also a second-year player, has been healthy for weeks after missing the start of the season, yet the team has been cautious about activating him. Head coach Klint Kubiak indicated the final call on Thornton will wait until Wednesday, the deadline by which the Raiders must either promote him or keep him on injured reserve for the rest of the year. Don't let the home team's offensive struggles fool you, though, as this remains one of the premier clubs in the NFL. Head coach Mike Macdonald's group might have the game's best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seahawks' defense is in the conversation for being football's most elite unit once again. Kansas City has its work cut out for it in what could be a tough road game, but one thing this year's team has shown is an abundance of grit. Will Sunday Night Football be more of the same? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 7 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Between the Seahawks’ offensive inconsistencies and the Chiefs’ offensive injuries, this feels like a low-scoring, wire-to-wire affair between two teams with elite elements in some areas and significant questions in others. Ultimately, fitting the narrative of the week perfectly, Kenneth Walker should be the key to this game for both teams. Jordan Foote: Going into Seattle and securing a win is easily the toughest ask of the Chiefs through the first month-and-a-half of the season. The Seahawks' defense, even while banged up, is amazing. On the other side of the ball, however, there's next to no run game. That's had a negative impact on quarterback Sam Darnold, who also isn't sniffing the production he found a season ago. Week 7's tilt could go either way, but I'll side with the offense I believe in much more. Minus wideout Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore , look for this one to be a statement game for one or both of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker III in hostile territory. Joshua Schulman: Kenneth Walker is set to return to face the franchise he won a Super Bowl with less than nine months ago, and he'll be looking to make his former team regret letting him walk. He and Jaxon Smith-Njigba headline one of the most exciting Sunday Night Football contests in recent memory. There's a generational quarterback in Patrick Mahomes squaring off against a generational defense that has picked up where it left off a season ago, despite the offense's inconsistencies. Seattle's slow start has actually placed it out of the playoff picture, and a home loss before another prime-time showdown against the Bears would be disastrous. I think the Seahawks understand the importance of this matchup and will take advantage of their 10 days of rest. Given the Chiefs' shaky kicking game and a lack of proven offensive weapons outside of Walker in what should be a low-scoring contest, I think Mike Macdonald and Co. narrowly steal one to hand Kansas City its first loss. Tyler Brown: This one has the look of a defensive rock fight. Seattle’s passing defense ranks first in the NFL, allowing just 141 yards per game, and Kansas City’s defense has held opponents under 20 points in most of its wins. The ingredients are there for a low-scoring grind from start to finish. That said, the Chiefs are the number one offense in the NFL for a reason. Seattle’s defense may be able to slow down Walker or Mahomes, but doing both simultaneously is a different ask entirely. If the run game gets going, the play-action attack opens up. If Mahomes starts finding his receivers, the box opens up for Walker. At some point, one of those two is going to win. On the other side, if Sam Darnold can buy time in the pocket, Smith-Njigba is going to get loose. The Chiefs’ defense just has to make sure that happens once or twice rather than repeatedly. away.headline: Chiefs cool Hill reunion: Andy Reid says nothing is happening; injury timeline clouds return
away.source: The Times of India on MSN
away.blurb: Tyreek Hill’s potential return to the Kansas City Chiefs has hit a significant roadblock, leaving fans wondering whether the explosive wide receiver will wear the red and gold again. What once looked like a promising reunion has lost momentum as concerns over his recovery continue to shape the conversation. With the Chiefs winning games and Patrick Mahomes leading the offence, Kansas City faces a difficult choice: take a chance on a familiar star or trust the players already on the roster. For Hill, the bigger challenge remains proving he can return to the field at his best. Without a clear medical assessment and a confirmed return timeline, Kansas City may be unwilling to take that risk. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! Why the Chiefs are hesitant to sign Tyreek Hill However, Hill’s health remains the biggest obstacle. The 32-year-old suffered a dislocated left knee and multiple ligament tears while playing for the Miami Dolphins during Week 4 of the 2025 NFL season. His injury required two surgeries, making his road back to professional football particularly challenging. Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has offered encouraging updates about his client’s rehabilitation and readiness to explore opportunities with NFL teams. Yet positive training reports cannot replace the medical assessments teams need before committing to a player recovering from such a serious injury. Hill built his reputation on elite speed, sharp changes of direction and the ability to turn short passes into game-changing plays. Those qualities make him dangerous, but they also raise questions about how quickly he can regain his previous form. Andy Reid’s Tyreek Hill update offers little hope of a reunion The comments suggest Kansas City is not preparing to rush into a deal, despite the team's earlier need for additional receiving options. Mahomes has also given the Chiefs reason to remain patient. He has started the 2026 campaign strongly, distributing the ball to targets such as Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. That production gives the coaching staff less reason to disrupt its current offensive plans for a player whose availability remains uncertain. Roster planning is another consideration. Bringing Hill back would require the team to assess his conditioning, recovery progress and ability to handle the demands of an NFL season. Promoting players who already understand Reid’s system could offer a more straightforward solution. Still, the situation could change if Kansas City suffers more injuries or Hill receives medical clearance sooner than expected. For now, Hill remains a free agent, and the Chiefs appear content to move forward without him. A reunion is not impossible, but the former Kansas City star must first overcome the uncertainty surrounding his recovery before any serious move becomes realistic. NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport reported the development Sunday morning, Oct. 25. And the news is particularly welcome considering Seattle's mounting injuries elsewhere on defense. The 22-year-old has already recorded 23 tackles and two sacks in five appearances this season, including 20 tackles over his past three games. Emmanwori has steadily regained his prominent defensive role after undergoing ankle surgery before training camp. Meanwhile, Nwosu has registered 15 tackles, one sack, three passes defended and a forced fumble through six games. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) did not participate in practice again after entering the concussion protocol during the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Moore’s participation going forward is dependent on the contracted independent neurologist and completely out of the team and player’s hands. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a limited participant in practice again. Kelce briefly left in Week 6 against the Chargers and was seen multiple times having his ankle taped. Linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) was a limited participant in practice for the second straight day. McDonald was placed on the team’s Reserve/Injured list after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. The Chiefs seemingly opened a roster spot for McDonald by waiving linebacker Cam Jones on Tuesday. Starting outside linebacker Uchenne Nwosu (hip) popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant after not appearing on the list on Wednesday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Dallas has dropped two straight games, but Philadelphia enters the NFC East matchup without Jalen Hurts Imagn Images In the Week 7 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Philadelphia Eagles play host to the division rival Dallas Cowboys . Philadelphia has lost four consecutive games after starting the season 2-0, and enters this game ravaged by injuries. Not only is Jalen Hurts out in the wake of blood clots being found in his calf and lungs, but DeVonta Smith , Dontayvion Wicks , Nolan Smith and more will also miss the game, while Saquon Barkley , Landon Dickerson , Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt are all questionable. Dallas has lost back-to-back games in dispiriting fashion, with its offense sputtering at the worst possible time, combining for 29 points against the Buccaneers and Packers after scoring 30-plus in each of the previous three games. The defense was already under fire early in the season, and now the Cowboys have questions on the side of the ball where they were supposed to be elite. Which of these two teams will stop their losing skid? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Eagles vs. Cowboys live Date: Monday, Oct. 26 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Lincoln Financial Field (Philadelphia) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Cowboys -4.5, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Cowboys have the ball Dallas has struggled badly on offense over the last two weeks. The Cowboys did total over 300 yards against both the Buccaneers and the Packers, but those totals are misleading. They were entirely unable to deal with blitzes for essentially all of both contests, and that failure brutally undermined their passing attack. ( Dak Prescott , typically excellent against blitzing defenses, went just 20 of 38 for 194 scoreless yards when confronting extra rushers in those games.) They also ran the ball for a mere 98 yards combined in those two games, despite the fact that star guard Tyler Smith returned to the fold. The struggles came a bit as a surprise considering the Cowboys had previously been cooking offensively, racking up yardage and points through the first four weeks of the season. But both Todd Bowles and Jonathan Gannon came out with a plan that toyed with Dallas' protection rules up front, and the Cowboys found themselves unable to respond. They'll need a significantly better plan on Monday night, but it's notable that the Eagles blitz far less often than the Bucs and Packers did against the Cowboys. The Bucs and Packers sent extra rushers after Prescott on 38.8% of his dropbacks in Weeks 5 and 6, per Tru Media. The Eagles have blitzed just 24.1% of the time so far - the fourth-lowest rate in the NFL . Vic Fangio would have to significantly depart from his modus operandi for Philadelphia to employ a strategy similar to the one that dominated Dallas over the last two weeks. For what it's worth, Philly has blitzed on at least 38% of opponent dropbacks just once since Fangio became the team's defensive coordinator. It would be wildly out of character to break out such a strategy here - but it's one worth pursuing considering Dallas' struggles. Philly checks in 20th in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, allowing opponents to complete only 60.4% of passes at an average of 7.0 yards per attempt, but giving up eight touchdown passes against just three interceptions and being helped along by 14 opponent drops - second-most in the league. Cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell , Riq Woolen and Cooper DeJean are tough to beat, but they have also been asked to cover for too long on some dropbacks because of the Eagles' inability to generate pressure. Philly has gotten a sack, hit or hurry on only 32.9% of opponent dropbacks, and they rank below-average in both average time to pressure and average time to throw. Quarterbacks, in other words, have been fairly comfortable in the pocket. And if you let Prescott get comfortable in the pocket, he can pick you apart with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , among his other targets. The Cowboys seem highly unlikely to find success running the ball, which they haven't done all year. Javonte Williams has seven rushing touchdowns, but he's also averaging only 3.7 yards per carry, down considerably from his 4.8 average last season. The offensive line is not clearing rushing lanes for him, and he's not making anybody miss to make up for it. It's a brutal combination, and with Philly allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, it's not an advantageous one here. When the Eagles have the ball The Eagles enter this game just about as banged up as possible on offense. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is out. His top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, are also out. Guard Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve, though he has been designated to return and listed as questionable for this game. Running back Saquon Barkley is questionable as well, and his top two backups — Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley — are on injured reserve. Without Hurts under center last week, the Eagles operated with a pass-heavy bent. Tanner McKee dropped back to throw 48 times, and while some of that was due to game script and some of it due to Barkley's absence, it's worth noting that he had previously made two Week 18 starts and dropped back to pass an average of 44 times in those games as well. The Eagles can't use the quarterback run game with McKee under center like they can with Hurts, and the rest of their run-game efficiency is likely to suffer as a result of not presenting that threat to the defense. It's somewhat reasonable to expect them to be pass-heavier than we're used to here. That may not be the case if Barkley returns to the lineup, but it is at least somewhat difficult to parse what the Eagles would prefer to do in that situation. Barkley has actually averaged 5.5 yards per carry in each of the two games he's made it through healthy this season. The problem is that the rest of the backs have been extremely inefficient in his absence and he wasn't efficient before leaving the other two games due to injury, either. He fully practiced on Friday for the first time since his hamstring injury, but the team may not want to load him up with too many touches in his first game back in the fold. Every team that is humanly capable of running the football (i.e., not the Texans or Packers) has done so at will against the Cowboys this season, with Dallas' other five opponents each piling up at least 165 yards on the ground. Opponents have clipped the Cowboys for 4.7 yards per carry, with running backs and quarterbacks alike able to find considerable room to run against a disappointingly friendly Dallas front. If the Eagles can get Barkley (or Dameon Pierce ) going early, they might be able to lean on the Cowboys and prevent the game from turning into the kind of track meet that Dallas' offense would prefer. Opponents have also generally been able to throw all over the Cowboys, though it will obviously be difficult for the Eagles to do so while down their top two receivers and multiple of their expected starting offensive linemen. It'll be Makai Lemon , Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert as McKee's top targets here. It'll be interesting to see if the Cowboys send Joey Porter Jr . to follow one of Cooper (who plays outside) or Lemon (usually in the slot, where he would match up more often with Caleb Downs ), as well as how they align their secondary now that Cobie Durant is set to return and potentially push the struggling (to say it kindly) Daron Bland to the bench. If the Cowboys can put any semblance of pressure on McKee, he could struggle badly. He's just 16 of 45 for 179 scoreless yards in his career when under duress, with a 15.1% sack rate as well. The Cowboys don't rush the passer particularly well, but with the current state of Philly's offensive line, that could change on Monday night. I just don't think the Cowboys should be favored by more than a field goal against anybody right now, given how they're playing on both sides of the ball. I'll take Dallas to win given the state of the Eagles' offense, but I can't see the Cowboys blowing anyone out in their current state. The Cowboys and Eagles were viewed as the best teams in the division going into the season, yet they are both trailing the New York Giants, who look like the least dysfunctional team in the NFC East after seven weeks. away.blurb: Hurts continued to receive treatment and monitoring before being ruled out of the Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers. What Happened to Jalen Hurts? Latest on Why He’s Out for Cowboys Matchup On October 9, Hurts received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the injury report ahead of the team’s trip to London. The following day, after the flight and the Eagles’ walkthrough, an ultrasound was performed out of an abundance of caution. The Eagles announced that Hurts had been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary emboli. His condition requires anticoagulation therapy, which involves taking blood thinners. Because these medications carry a significant risk of bleeding, Hurts cannot have physical contact, potentially sidelining him for three or more months and out for the remainder of the 2026 season. Black clouds continue to loom over the Philadelphia Eagles’ quarterback room as Jalen Hurts deals with a medical situation. Ahead of the Week 7 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, the team’s medical staff and head coach Nick Sirianni have offered more insight into the QB’s status. The injury concerns began on October 4, when the Eagles faced the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4. Hurts reportedly took a cleat to his left calf during the game but continued playing. Four days later, after practicing in full, Hurts requested treatment for his calf and told the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Medical staff cleared Hurts to play, concluding that activity and mobility were important. The Eagles said he played without limitation against Jacksonville before flying back to Philadelphia with the team. away.headline: Cowboys-Eagles final injury update has 7 ruled out including Smith
away.blurb: Running back Saquon Barkley is on track to appear for the first time since leaving the Week 4 game early, and should bring a huge boost to a running game that has floundered the last three weeks. Hopefully ready to meet him in the hole is linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who hasn't seen action since Week 1 for the Cowboys. The Cowboys also expect CB Cobie Durant to return to action, and he hasn't played since Week 2. Those are two big additions for Dallas. Things are trending right for several other Cowboys, though they aren't quite ready to return to action. The Cowboys opened the 21-day practice window for LB Marist Liufau and safety PJ Locke. Both were expected to be key reserves this year and still could be activated before Monday's game, with corresponding roster moves. Starting safety Jalen Thompson can have his window opened next week. Meanwhile, Dallas did rule out WR/KR Kavontae Turpin (ribs) and LB Dee Winters (calf), along with OT Drew Shelton. McKee won't have his top two receivers as both DeVonta Smith and Dontarin Wycks have been ruled out. Barkley is one of seven listed as questionable, along with OF Landon Dickerson and edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who is expected to be a game-time decision . Entering their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup, the teams sport identical 2-4 records after six games , with injuries the underlying factor of both club's malaise. Dallas, implementing a new defense under first-year coordinator Christian Parker, has seen their back-seven progressively decimated week by week, undermining his attempt to get his footing as a scheme designer and playcaller. The Eagles have just lost body after body throughout their roster, losing key contributors to the offense. Are the clubs trending in opposite directions despite losing streaks for both ? Injury wise, Dallas is starting to get some contributors back, with the question being about whether they can actually make a difference or is Parker's scheme a bad one. The Eagles are trending down, still, though they will get a big boost from one returning member. For Philly, the injury discussion has centered around QB Jalen Hurts and the controversy over his blood clot diagnosis . Regardless of the inner workings there, he's been moved to IR and is done for the year, opening the door for Tanner McKee to get the start and raising the possibility if he flounders, the Eagles could turn to Joe Milton III at QB. Philly snatched him off of Dallas' practice squad last week . Here's a look at the complete injury report from Saturday.

home.headline: Cowboys vs. Eagles Injury Report
home.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys.
